title: validator_set_at edge validity is evaluated against a set that changes at a node-local time; a departing author's round-(a+1) vote poisons every cone that cited it before the node executed anchor a, permanently, and halts the chain at n<=6
which_invariant: §3's own admission rule ('pure function of the vertex bytes plus state identical on every node') and I9-style determinism; v2 #5/#6/#9 class (node-local state deciding validity), the exact class the author claims v3 closed
design_section: §3 (edge check 'parent.author ∈ validator_set_at(parent.round)'), §3.2 (snapshot 'keyed by the anchor round at which it took effect', used by ingress :1082 and by the walk), §3.4 ('admitted everywhere and resolves nowhere — deterministic')
attack:
Setup verified at HEAD: the set is rewritten only inside block execution of the anchor's block (executor append_validator_removal core/executor/src/lib.rs:866-912; slash removal :2532-2580), so `sys:validator_set_at:a` exists on a node only after that node has executed anchor a. Anchor a commits DIRECTLY only when >2/3 of round-(a+1) bodies citing L_a are held (ordering.rs:558-567, direct_quorum_met :655-680), and try_commit runs inside add_vertex (dag.rs:1290) AFTER the round advance to quorum_round+1 (dag.rs:1226-1232), which fires as soon as >2/3 of round-(a+1) AUTHORS are held, votes or not. The 3 s ticker (core/node/src/main.rs:679-686) builds round a+2 from round_index[a+1] whenever current_round == a+2.

Sequence (n=4: honest A,B,C + M; M is removed at anchor a by slash or voluntary leave):
1. Every node builds and admits M_{a+1} under the pre-removal set (nobody has executed a yet — a's commit REQUIRES the a+1 round). M_{a+1} is a valid, signed, in-set body on every node.
2. M's a+1 vertex does not cite L_a (a slashed Byzantine M omits it deliberately; an honest leaver omits it with the ordinary 5 % loss of L_a). On any node where M_{a+1} is among the first three a+1 arrivals, current_round advances to a+2 while a is not yet directly committable (2 votes of 4). The ticker fires in the gap (up to ~3 s, the spread of the other nodes' tickers) and that node builds X_{a+2} citing [A,B,C,M]_{a+1} — all Resolved under the pre-removal set. P(taint per honest node) ≈ 0.5; P(≥1 of 3 tainted) ≈ 0.87.
3. The fourth a+1 vote arrives; every node commits a, executes the block, writes `sys:validator_set_at:a` = set∖M. From this instant, on EVERY node, the edge X_{a+2} → M_{a+1} fails 'parent.author ∈ validator_set_at(a+1)'. Per §3 this verdict is not Unresolved{blocked_on} — it is invalid, it has no blocked_on hash, and no trigger in §3's list ((a) admission, (b) sync settlement, (c) tick re-walk) can ever flip it. Every vertex whose cone contains X_{a+2} resolves nowhere forever (floor-0 walk descends every held uncommitted edge).
4. Round a+3: R4 uses the CURRENT set (§3.2), now 3 validators; `stake_quorum_met` is strict (qc.rs:194-196: 3·signed > 2·total ⇒ all 3 honest a+2 bodies must be clean). One tainted a+2 body ⇒ no honest node reaches R4 at a+3 ⇒ no a+3 vertices ⇒ anchor a+2 never gets direct votes ⇒ nothing is ever committed above a ⇒ M_{a+1} and X_{a+2} never enter committed_set (the only way the walk would stop examining that edge) ⇒ no block ⇒ no sync adoption ⇒ the below-quorum re-gossip branch (dag.rs:881-926) re-sends bodies everyone already holds. Permanent halt with no fetchable hole. A slashed equivocator's last vertex therefore halts the chain at its own slash anchor with ~87 % probability at n=4; the tolerance is f < n/3 tainted builders.

Milder, honest-only variant at larger n: a node that lost L_a (5 %) cannot commit a until a+2's ancestry decides it (ordering.rs:583-597), builds a+2 and a+3 citing M_{a+1}/its own chain, and after executing a via sync it can no longer resolve its OWN previous vertices; its output for those rounds is excluded from every honest cone — silent exclusion, exactly what §4's 'byte-identical sequences' criterion was added to catch, but a 4-node honest burn-in never changes the set, so the gate cannot see it.

Same root cause as v2 #6/#9 (ingress :1082 reads the current set), which v3 marks fixed: `validator_set_at(round)` keyed by the removal anchor is identical across nodes only for rounds ≤ the last anchor every node has executed; for the two rounds where the departing author's bodies actually exist it is the current set on some nodes and the new set on others.
design_fix:
Membership must be evaluated against a set that every honest node provably had before any honest node could have built the citing vertex, and 'not known yet' must be a deferral, never an invalidation:
1. Define validator_set_at(p) := the set after executing all anchors ≤ p − Δ with Δ ≥ 2 (rounds a+1 of a departing author remain valid citations on every node, since a+1 bodies are always built before anchor a executes; a+2 bodies are invalid for everyone and cited by nobody because no node cites round-(a+2) parents before round a+3, by which point the verdict below applies).
2. If the anchor ≤ p − Δ has not been executed locally, the edge verdict is Unresolved{blocked_on_anchor: that anchor}, never Invalid; add a fourth release trigger: anchor execution re-walks entries blocked on that anchor round (O(dependents), same index as (a)/(b)).
3. Ingress (:1082) must NOT reject on validator_set_at for rounds inside the uncommitted window — membership there is not decidable identically; keep signature + resolve_author_pubkey and a per-author byte bound (I11) as the ingress defence, and let the walk decide.
4. Keep the newest `sys:validator_set_at` row regardless of the prune horizon (§4 says rows are 'pruned with the DAG horizon'; pruning the only row makes set_at(p) undefined for every p).
5. Add the test the mutation catalogue lacks: `departing_author_vote_cited_pre_execution_does_not_halt` — 4 validators, leave/slash at anchor a, M_{a+1} omits L_a, one node builds a+2 before executing a; assert a+2 and a+4 commit with identical anchor_hash on all nodes. Mutation: key the edge check on the removal anchor (Δ=0).

title: A real body delivered to one honest node is the same wedge as a fake hash: Stage 1 alone lets one Byzantine key permanently exclude any honest validator and halt n=4 with two ordinary-looking vertices
which_invariant: I1/I2 ('no mechanism may require a node to already hold data in order to obtain it') — Stage 1 has no obtain mechanism at all; §0/§1 claim Part I 'closes the malicious wedge' and §11 claims Stage 1 is shippable alone
design_section: §3.4 'Consequence for the malicious case' (traces only a parent that hashes nothing), §1, §4 exit criterion, §11 Stage 1 gate, §12 'R4 stops a lagging node from proposing — intended'
attack:
Verified: parents are cited by bare hash from round_index[prev] (dag.rs:527-536), a node cites its OWN previous vertex (own vertex enters round_index via add_vertex at dag.rs:749), ingress does not examine parents (dag.rs:948-1083), the only redelivery is the below-quorum push of dag.values() within current_round−3 (dag.rs:881-926), and votes are counted from held bodies regardless of resolution (direct_quorum_met ordering.rs:655-680).

Sequence (validators A,B,C honest, M Byzantine, equal stake):
1. Round k: M builds X_k with perfectly valid edges (cites the honest k−1 bodies) and delivers it ONLY to A (direct TCP to A, no gossip). No equivocation, no fake hash, nothing slashable.
2. A: resolve_walk(X_k) = Resolved (edges valid, ancestors held). A cites X_k in A_{k+1}. B, C admit A_{k+1} but resolve_walk(A_{k+1}) = Unresolved{X_k}. No trigger ever fires: X_k is never admitted on B/C (nobody re-sends it: A is above quorum and never enters the re-gossip branch; M won't) and never enters committed_set (X_k is in a cone only via A's chain; no non-A vertex ever cites an A vertex ≥ k+1 because every A vertex cites its own predecessor, so A's chain is unresolvable on B/C forever; A's leader rounds get only A's own vote and are skipped).
3. From k+1 on, A's entire output is outside consensus on every other node (its transactions never commit, its leader slots are skipped) while A itself sees nothing wrong. B and C continue at 3/4 > 2/3 while M keeps proposing.
4. Round m: M delivers X'_m only to B. Now C resolves only C and M at m+2 (2/4, strict >2/3 fails, qc.rs:194-196) → C silent. M stops proposing (or simply cites only C and M). A resolves A,(C,M chains) → proposes; B likewise; next round each of A and B sees only itself + M's stale round → below quorum. All honest nodes silent; quorum_round (dag.rs:493-525) stops advancing; the re-gossip windows (current−3) no longer cover X_k or X'_m; no anchor gains votes; no block; no sync. Permanent halt, two vertices, no evidence.

HEAD halts on the same input through the commit hole (B/C cite A_{k+1}, walk_history :697-702 → None), so Part I does not make this worse — it simply does not close the class it names. §3.4 is the 'unaffected' claim of this round: it traces the fake-hash instance and generalises to 'the malicious wedge'. The Stage 1 exit gate (§4: honest 4-node burn-in) cannot observe it, and §12 files the mechanism that would rescue it (pull from a holder) under Part II.
design_fix: Either do not claim Stage 1 is shippable alone, or give Stage 1 the minimum obtain path: (1) a bounded pull for hashes that are cited by a held body and absent (the WANTED Tier-A/Tier-B core of §5, without shadow/equivocation), gated as part of Stage 1; or (2) a Stage-1-only fallback: the below-quorum re-gossip branch re-sends not `dag.values()` in a 4-round window but the bodies of every hash in the node's own Unresolved{blocked_on} sets that it DOES hold, and holders re-send on request… which is a pull. There is no Stage 1 without I2. Add the test `selectively_delivered_valid_vertex_does_not_exclude_receiver` (X_k to A only; assert A's k+3 vertex is in the committed sequence on B and C within 8 ticks) and put it in the Stage 1 gate; mutation: remove the pull.

title: R4 (proposer, CURRENT set) and R4′ (commit, validator_set_at(round−1)) are different thresholds; at a set change one lost parent makes an honestly-built leader vertex 'defer, never skip' forever — a wedge sync cannot clear
which_invariant: §3.1's premise ('every vertex at j+2 references >2/3 of the j+1 vertices', ordering.rs:513-517) — restored only if proposer and committer measure >2/3 against the same denominator; I1 (commit path must never stall on an admitted honest vertex)
design_section: §3.1 (parent_quorum_met over the current set), §3.2 ('the current set is still used for parent_quorum_met … unchanged'), §3.3 R4′ ('> 2/3 of validator_set_at(round − 1) … otherwise it defers … never skipped')
attack:
Verified: parent_quorum_met uses get_validator_set_with_stake() (dag.rs:545-585), the set is rewritten only at block execution (executor :810-912, :2532-2580), a node can build a+2 before executing a (round advance dag.rs:1226-1232 precedes the commit at :1290 and needs authors, not votes), and step 1 of try_commit takes the smallest directly committable anchor ≥ cursor with no other exit (ordering.rs:558-571).

Sequence (voluntary leave of V at anchor a, 4 equal validators → 3):
1. The round-(a+2) leader L builds L_{a+2} before executing a (M_{a+1} or V_{a+1} arrived among the first three and did not vote, see hole 1; or L simply lost L_a and cannot commit a until a+2's ancestry). Its R4 denominator is the OLD set (100): it cites three of four a+1 bodies (one lost, 5 %), including V_{a+1} — 75 % > 2/3, passes, proposes.
2. Every node later executes a (directly, or by ancestry once a+2 has votes) and evaluates R4′ for L_{a+2} against validator_set_at(a+1) = {A,B,C} (75): present parent authors in that set = 2 → 50/75 = 66.7 %, strictly-greater fails (qc.rs:194-196). Same arithmetic for a join with equal stake: 3/4 old = 75 % passes R4, 3/5 new = 60 % fails R4′.
3. §3.3: 'Otherwise it defers (returns empty); it is never skipped by proof.' Step 1 on every node stops at a+2 and returns empty; the cursor never advances; nothing above a is ever committed on any node; sync adoption cannot help because no node produces a block for a+2 or beyond. Permanent wedge from an honest leave and one lost gossip message, on every node identically (so §4's 'identical sequences' burn-in reads green right up to the stall). Note L_{a+2} DOES get direct votes at a+3 from nodes that resolved it (those that also built pre-execution), so the stall is not the 'no votes' case that the skip handles.
design_fix: Proposer and committer must apply the same predicate to the same data: make parent_quorum_met use validator_set_at(round − 1) with the Δ-lagged definition from hole 1 (so the proposer can always evaluate it and the committer evaluates the identical set), and make R4′ a pure function of that same function. Then any honest vertex that passed R4 passes R4′ on every node. Additionally, R4′ must not be a permanent 'defer' for a vertex that HAS direct votes: if direct_quorum_met is true for a sub-quorum-present leader, the missing parent is a hole (defer until settled) not a policy failure — merge R4′ into the existing completeness gate (commit_one_anchor :731) rather than a separate eligibility rule. Test: `leader_built_under_old_set_is_eligible_under_new_set` — leave at a, leader builds a+2 pre-execution citing the leaver plus two others; assert a+2 commits on all nodes; mutation: R4′ on the current-round set.

title: committed_set is not 'state identical on every node': a leader-signed block with an empty vertices_root carries an unverified committed_vertices list, so sync-settled nodes and locally-committed nodes reach opposite verdicts for the same bytes
which_invariant: §3's determinism premise ('state identical on every node'); I8 (sync settlement must release exactly as gossip settlement does — it must also settle exactly the same hashes); I1
design_section: §2 S2 SETTLED ('H ∈ committed_set; body may be absent … via dag.rs:2852-2884'), §3 cache trigger (b) ('enters committed_set via sync adoption'), §3.4
attack:
Verified at HEAD: ChainSync checks `vertices_root` only `if !block.header.vertices_root.is_empty()` (sync/src/lib.rs:290-297); the header hash likewise folds vertices_root only when non-empty (blockchain/src/lib.rs:292-293), so an empty root is a legitimately signable header; the proposer signature is verified (sync/src/lib.rs:366) but binds nothing about committed_vertices when the root is empty; reload_chain_tip adopts `block.committed_vertices` verbatim into committed_set whenever it is non-empty and the block is signed (dag.rs:2870-2880 → adopt_synced_anchor ordering.rs:869-888).

Sequence:
1. Byzantine M is the leader of anchor a (every n-th anchor). M publishes V_r citing fake P at some earlier round; per §3.4, P is Unresolved everywhere, nobody cites V_r. Fine so far.
2. M signs block h for anchor a with vertices_root = "" and committed_vertices = honest sequence ∪ {P, V_r} (or just P). Honest validators that committed a locally build their own block h and never look at M's (dedup dag.rs:1305-1312). Any node that obtains height h by ChainSync — a restarted validator, a lagging follower (the very node §3 trigger (b) exists for), every observer/indexer — accepts M's block: signature valid, root check skipped, sequence adopted verbatim.
3. On those nodes P ∈ committed_set. resolve_walk(V_r) and of every later M vertex chained on it returns Resolved (the walk stops at committed hashes before examining them, ordering.rs:708-710). The synced validator cites M's chain; its vertices resolve nowhere on the locally-committed validators (P is a hole there) — the same bytes, opposite verdicts, decided by which peer served block h. Its commit walk of any anchor containing M's chain succeeds while the majority's defers, and its block h already differs in hash from the honest block h, so it is forked at the block level with a poisoned settled predicate that no later honest block can unpoison (committed_set only grows).

The design treats 'sync adoption' as a trusted settlement path equal to local commit (S2 'commit / sync'), but at HEAD the adopted list is bound to the header only when the producer chose to bind it.
design_fix: Settlement via sync must be as verified as settlement via commit: (1) make vertices_root mandatory whenever committed_vertices is non-empty — reject at sync/src/lib.rs:290 if the root is empty but the list is not, and fold the root into the header hash unconditionally (bump the header format); (2) in adopt_synced_anchor, refuse any hash that is neither held in `dag` nor already in committed_set unless the block's QC (>2/3 finality votes) is present for that height — a single proposer signature is not consensus; (3) require the adopted anchor_hash to be the leader_for_round(anchor_round) author's vertex when the body is held. Add `forged_sync_sequence_cannot_settle_unheld_hash` to the Part I test plan: leader-signed block with empty root and an extra hash; assert the follower's committed_set does not contain it; mutation: skip the root check when empty.

title: R4' 'defers' on a fully resolvable sub-quorum leader vertex: one signed vertex with one valid parent halts every node permanently; HEAD commits it fine
attack: Attacker holds one validator key D and leads even round j (leader_for_round is a pure function of the round and set, ordering.rs:641-646). (1) D publishes D_{j-1} normally (cites >2/3, resolvable everywhere). (2) D publishes D_j with parents = [D_{j-1}] only. Ingress accepts it: parents non-empty, unique, hash/signature valid (dag.rs:1046-1076); nothing at ingress checks parent quorum, by design (section 3.3 'Ingress keeps only what is a pure function of bytes'). (3) Every honest resolve_walk(D_j) returns Some: the single edge D_j -> D_{j-1} is round-exact, the author is a member, and D_{j-1} resolves. R1 checks resolvability, not parent quorum. So every honest node cites D_j at round j+1 (R4 cites all resolved round-j vertices). (4) try_commit step 1 (ordering.rs:554-567): leader_vertex_hash(j) = D_j; direct_quorum_met = A,B,C votes = 75% > 2/3 -> true. R4' (section 3.3): present-parent stake of D_j = D's 25% <= 2/3 -> not anchor-eligible -> 'it defers (returns empty)'. (5) Every later try_commit call re-evaluates the same cursor with the same complete state: nothing is missing, nothing will ever arrive, so the deferral is permanent on every node simultaneously. No anchor >= j, no block, no sync. Global permanent halt from one vertex that is not even malformed under R1. At HEAD the same vertex commits normally: commit_one_anchor's floor-0 walk (ordering.rs:731-737) completes through D_{j-1}. Part I introduces this halt. The design is also self-contradictory: section 3.4 and test row 5 ('one_parent_leader_not_eligible ... skipped identically within 2 anchors') expect a SKIP, but section 3.3's text says defer, and a vertex that is in `visited` (step 2, ordering.rs:583-597) can only be skipped if ineligibility is defined as 'treat as absent', which the text never says.
which_invariant: I1 (the commit path must never encounter an undecidable round from an admitted vertex); the section 3.3 claim 'a parentless or sub-quorum vertex can therefore never anchor and never prove a skip' is true and is exactly the problem: it can never be skipped either
design_fix: Define ineligibility as equivalence with 'no leader vertex at that round': in step 1 an ineligible leader vertex is scanned past exactly like a missing one; in step 2, when the walk from the chain anchor is complete, an ineligible leader vertex is SKIPPED whether or not it is in `visited`; never return empty on eligibility alone. State explicitly that eligibility is computed on node-local present bodies and that this is safe only because commit_one_anchor's floor-0 gate (ordering.rs:731-737) prevents a node that lacks the leader's parent bodies from committing the NEXT anchor either (it would hit the same hole), so a divergent skip decision can never be persisted; then add the test 'sub_quorum_leader_with_resolvable_parent_is_skipped_not_deferred' with the mutation 'return empty when ineligible', and fix row 5's assertion to match.

title: R4 without a pull: one lost gossip vertex ejects a validator from proposing; two concurrent ejections halt the chain permanently with zero Byzantine nodes
attack: n=4 {A,B,C,X}, equal stake, all honest, ordinary gossip loss. (1) Round r-1: X loses D... call the lost vertex A_{r-1}. X still resolves {B,C,X}_{r-1} = 75% > 2/3 and proposes X_r. (2) A, B, C hold A_{r-1} and, per R4, cite every resolved round-(r-1) vertex, so A_r, B_r, C_r all cite A_{r-1} (dag.rs:529-536 cites round_index[prev] verbatim; the design keeps that, filtered by resolvability). (3) Round r+1 on X: resolve_walk(A_r/B_r/C_r) with floor 0 (section 3) descends into A_{r-1} -> not in dag, not committed, not genesis -> Unresolved{A_{r-1}}. X's only resolved candidate is its own X_r = 25%. R4: X does not propose. (4) X's current_round is still dragged forward by peers' vertices (dag.rs:1231-1239 fast-forwards to quorum_round+1 from PRESENT stake, not resolved stake), so at every later round X's candidates all transitively cite A_{r-1}; the tick re-walk (section 3 cache rule (c)) re-walks and fails identically. (5) Nothing delivers A_{r-1}: the only redelivery is the below-quorum push of dag.values() (dag.rs:881-926) executed by the node that LACKS the vertex; A holds it and is above quorum, so never pushes. X is ejected until a synced block settles A_{r-1} via adopt_synced_anchor (dag.rs:2871-2878). (6) Now B independently loses one vertex at round r (P ~ 1-0.95^3 = 14% per node per round at the design's own 5% loss row). B is ejected at r+1 the same way. Round r+1 now has only A_{r+1} and C_{r+1}: votes for L_r = 50%, direct_quorum_met (ordering.rs:650-676) false forever. (7) Round r+2: A resolves {A,C}_{r+1} = 50% -> R4 refuses; C likewise. No vertex is ever produced again; no anchor, no block, no ChainSync, so step (5)'s only rescue never fires. Permanent halt. At HEAD the same losses are harmless: parent_quorum_met counts PRESENT parents (dag.rs:566-585), X and B keep voting, anchors commit, and the commit-side holes are rescued by adoption. Part I is strictly worse than HEAD under routine loss; under the section 10 live row (5% loss, 4 nodes) the probability that >=2 of 4 nodes are ejected in the same round is ~10% per round, i.e. minutes to halt.
which_invariant: I2 (redelivery must be a PULL from a holder; no mechanism may require holding data to obtain it), I10 (re-entry from a gap larger than any re-gossip window); the design's own section 12 claim 'deferral, never wedge or fork' and section 9 row 'I10: tick re-walk while R4 fails'
design_section: 3.1 (R4), 3 cache rule (c), 4 exit criterion, 9 rows I2/I10, 12
design_fix: Part I cannot gate proposing on full-history resolvability without a pull. Either (a) move the minimal request/response of section 5.3 (VERTEX_REQ/VERTEX_RESP, direct TCP, bounded to blocked_on hashes of round-(r-1) candidates, asked of the candidate's author and of the validators with peer_ip) into Stage 1, so the below-quorum branch REQUESTS the blocked_on set instead of pushing what it already holds; or (b) keep HEAD's present-parent quorum for the decision to propose and apply R1 only as a citation filter with a hard rule that a node below resolved-quorum still proposes citing its resolved subset (which breaks the skip-proof premise, so (a) is the only option that preserves R4'). In both cases: define settled-without-body hashes (committed_set after adoption) as terminal for resolve_walk with no edge check, and add a burn-in metric 'rounds proposed per validator' with a floor, because the exit criterion 'identical sequences' is blind to a validator silently reduced to a sync-follower.

title: validator_set_at(round) is written by each node's own executor at its own time, so membership at ingress and in the R1 edge check is admit-here/reject-there; with n=4 one honest leave or slash halts the chain
attack: n=4 {A,B,C,D}, D voluntarily leaves; the removal is staged into anchor j's block batch (executor/src/lib.rs:866-912) and lands on each node when that node executes anchor j (dag.rs:1275-1290 loop). The design keys the snapshot 'sys:validator_set_at:{j}' to that execution (section 3.2), so validator_set_at(j+1) flips from {A,B,C,D} to {A,B,C} on each node at its own execution instant. (1) Deciding anchor j requires >2/3 of round-(j+1) votes (ordering.rs:650-676), so round j+1 and typically j+2 vertices, including D_{j+1}, are produced BEFORE any node executes anchor j; D itself keeps proposing until D executes j. (2) C finds direct quorum first, executes j, writes the snapshot; D_{j+1} arrives at C 200 ms later; ingress membership under validator_set_at(j+1) = {A,B,C} (section 3.2 says :1082 uses it) -> rejected, and permanently: every re-delivery is rejected the same way. A and B received D_{j+1} before executing j -> admitted. (3) A's proposal at j+2 races A's execution of j (both are triggered by the same round-(j+1) quorum, dag.rs:1231-1239 vs :1275-1290). A proposes first: resolve_walk(D_{j+1}) edge check passes (pre-execution set), cached Resolved 'authoritative until pruned' (section 3), so A_{j+2} cites D_{j+1}. (4) On C: resolve_walk(A_{j+2}) reaches D_{j+1}, absent and never admissible -> Unresolved forever. On B (executed j by now): the edge A_{j+2} -> D_{j+1} fails membership under the post-execution snapshot -> Unresolved forever (blocked on nothing). (5) Post-leave the set is {A,B,C}, and stake_quorum_met (qc.rs:194-196) with n=3 requires all three. At j+3, B and C resolve {B,C}_{j+2} = 2/3, not > 2/3 -> R4 refuses. Only A proposes at j+3. At j+4 every node resolves only A_{j+3} = 1/3 -> nobody proposes. Permanent halt, zero Byzantine participants, on every voluntary leave or slash at n=4. At HEAD the same ingress rejection (dag.rs:1078-1088, current set) also happens, but present-parent quorum keeps everyone proposing and voting, so anchors commit and C's commit hole is rescued by adoption; Part I converts a tolerated ingress non-determinism into a network halt. The design is also internally inconsistent: section 3 says membership is 'not an ingress rejection', section 3.2 says 'Ingress membership (:1082) ... use validator_set_at(vertex.round)'. Both readings fail: with the rejection you get the sequence above; without any membership gate at all, any key can insert unbounded vertices into dag and vertex:{H} (I3/I4).
which_invariant: I6 (any admitted signal must be true on every node alike) and the design's own section 3 principle 'admission must be a pure function of the vertex bytes plus state identical on every node' - validator_set_at(round) is not identical across nodes at the time a round-(j+1) or round-(j+2) vertex arrives; this is the v2 #5 class the author claims section 3.2 closes
design_section: 3.2, 3 (edge checks), 3 cache ('Resolved entry is authoritative until pruned')
design_fix: Make membership a WEIGHT, never a validity condition. Ingress admits any author that appears in any snapshot the node holds within the unpruned window (bounded per author by the existing per-key limits); it never rejects on the newest set alone. Remove author-membership from the R1 edge check (round-exactness stays). R4, R4' and direct_quorum_met already weight authors by the set at decision time, which is re-sampled per anchor on every node identically (dag.rs:1275-1290), so a non-member simply contributes 0 stake. Additionally, make set changes take effect at anchor_round + K rounds with K larger than the maximum number of rounds in flight before an anchor is executed (at least 4), so no honest vertex at an affected round can exist before every node has executed the change; document that the snapshot key is the EFFECTIVE round, not the executing anchor round.

title: Part I claims to close the malicious wedge, but one equivocating key still halts the chain permanently, now at the proposer where ChainSync cannot rescue it
attack: n=4 {A,B,C,D}; D holds one validator key. (1) Round r: D sends twin T1 to A and B and twin T2 to C (asymmetric delivery, the I9 scenario). On A and B the later-arriving T2 hits the equivocation branch (dag.rs:1132-1160): slash proof broadcast, return without insert; the sys:equiv_seen latch (dag.rs:2287-2290) means T2 is never admitted on A/B, and symmetrically T1 never on C. Part I has no shadow and no fetch. (2) Round r+1: A_{r+1}, B_{r+1} cite T1 (resolved on A, B); C_{r+1} cites T2; D withholds its own vote or cites T2. (3) Round r+2 on A: resolve_walk(C_{r+1}) -> edge to T2 -> not in dag, not committed, never admissible -> Unresolved forever; resolve_walk(D_{r+1}) likewise. A resolves {A,B}_{r+1} = 50% -> R4 refuses. B same. C resolves {C,D}_{r+1} = 50% -> refuses. (4) No vertex is ever produced at r+2 or later on any node; no votes for L_r (50% at most); no anchor, no block, no adoption. Permanent halt of the whole network from one key, no fake hash needed. This is the same attacker capability (one validator key) that section 3.4 says Part I neutralises; the outcome equals HEAD's commit wedge, but Part I moves it to the proposer so the only Part I recovery path (adopt_synced_anchor, dag.rs:2871-2878) can never fire, and none of the Part I gates (rows 1-7, 48 h honest burn-in) exercise it. Part I is therefore not 'shippable alone' against the threat it names in section 0.
which_invariant: I9 (equivocation must never create a citable-but-unobtainable hash); section 0's claim 'Part I ... closes the malicious wedge'
design_section: 0, 3.4, 4 (exit criterion), 11 Stage 1 gate
design_fix: Either state in section 0/11 that Stage 1 does not close single-key halts and that mainnet is gated on Stage 2-4, or pull the bounded shadow STORE of section 6 (one compact+parents row per (author, round), written after guards drop, read by resolve_walk as dag ∪ shadow) into Stage 1 without E1/E2, so both twins are resolvable on every node that receives both, and make the leader-round decision defer (not skip, not commit) whenever leader_vertex_hash finds more than one twin. Add a Part I adversarial row 'equivocation_2_2_does_not_stop_proposing' with the mutation 'drop the second twin at ingress'.

title: Test row 3 asserts convergence 'after redelivery' but Part I has no redelivery; the row is unpassable as specified and the exit criterion cannot observe proposer ejection
attack: Row 3 'sub_quorum_cited_parents_do_not_propose' requires: a node lacking the round-r leader vertex, leading r+2, enters the below-quorum branch, and 'peers and it converge after redelivery'. Trace the redelivery: the node lacking the vertex enters dag.rs:881-926 and pushes dag.values() for rounds >= current-3, i.e. everything EXCEPT the vertex it lacks; the holders are above parent quorum and never enter that branch; there is no VERTEX_REQ in Part I (section 0 'no messages, no WANTED'). The only way the node re-resolves is adopt_synced_anchor (dag.rs:2871-2878) placing the lost hash into committed_set, which requires the other three nodes to commit an anchor and produce a block. The row does not name adoption, so an implementer either (a) writes a test that passes only through ChainSync and calls the mutation 'quorum over present instead of cited' caught, or (b) cannot make it pass. Meanwhile the Part I exit criterion (section 4: identical committed sequences and anchor_hash per height on every node) is satisfied by a cluster in which one validator never proposes again and merely follows blocks - exactly hole #1's ejected state - so the burn-in is blind to the regression it introduces.
which_invariant: I2, I10; section 10's rule that each row must isolate the mutation that fails it
design_section: 10 row 3, 4 (exit criterion)
design_fix: Rewrite row 3 to name the recovery path explicitly (adoption via a synced block, or the Stage 1 pull if hole #1's fix (a) is taken) and to assert that the ejected node PROPOSES again within N rounds of that event with zero add_vertex calls for the lost hash. Add to the section 4 exit criterion: every validator proposes in >= 95% of rounds over the 48 h burn-in under the 5% loss profile; any validator silent for > 8 consecutive rounds fails the gate.

title: resolve_walk's edge check is undefined for settled-without-body parents: one reading permanently ejects every node that ever adopted a synced anchor, the other silently drops round-exactness
attack: Section 2 S2 says a settled hash 'may be absent' (committed_set via adopt_synced_anchor, ordering.rs:869-888 through dag.rs:2871-2878, folds the producer's sequence verbatim; the bodies are not delivered). Section 3 says every path must terminate in genesis or committed_set AND every edge child -> parent must satisfy parent.round == child.round - 1 and membership at parent.round. For a parent in committed_set with no body, parent.round and parent.author do not exist. Reading 1 (edge check applied before the settled stop): follower X adopts anchor r whose sequence contains the hash P it lost; X's re-walk of A_{r+1} reaches edge A_{r+1} -> P, cannot read P.round -> invalid -> Unresolved with empty blocked_on; hook (b) fires and fails; X never proposes again after its first adoption - every follower in the design's own burn-in (5% loss forces adoption regularly) is progressively ejected, feeding hole #1. Reading 2 (settled stop before the edge check): a vertex at round 500 may cite a committed round-2 hash and resolve; harmless for I1 but R4' then counts 'present parent bodies' without a round restriction unless specified, and the round-exactness premise that makes 'round-(r-1) candidates' well-defined for rule (c) and R4' is gone. The design does not choose, and the two readings have opposite liveness consequences.
which_invariant: I8 (a hash settled via sync must release dependents exactly as arrival does); I10
design_section: 2 (S2), 3 (edge checks and cache rule (b)), 3.3 (R4' 'present parent bodies')
design_fix: Specify: a parent hash in committed_set or equal to 'genesis' terminates the path with NO edge check (the committed prefix is the network's decision and needs no re-validation); round-exactness and any membership weighting apply only to edges whose parent body is held. Specify R4' as: distinct-author stake of held parent bodies whose round == anchor.round - 1, over the set used for the anchor decision. Add the test 'adopted_hole_rewalks_and_proposes_again' (ChainSync adoption only, zero add_vertex for the lost hash, node proposes within 2 rounds) with the mutation 'apply the edge check to settled parents'.

title: validator_set_at(round) is undefined for in-flight rounds, so it collapses to the CURRENT set — the exact local-state admission v3 claims to have removed; one slash/leave with n=4 halts the chain permanently
attack: Set changes are block-execution events: slash evidence applies at step 0 of execute_block_parallel_at (executor:1732, :2532-2590), join/leave are staged into the block batch (:3456-3475). The executor is only given block_height (:1675-1680). Committing anchor R requires the round-(R+1) votes (ordering.rs:663-686, :558-567), so at the instant block(R) executes on a node, vertices at R+1..R+3 are already in flight and were admitted on other nodes under the current set (dag.rs:1077-1088). No `sys:validator_set_at:{r}` row can exist for r > R at that moment on ANY node, so validator_set_at(R+2) must fall back to 'latest row <= r' — which is the pre-change set on a node that has not executed block(R) and the post-change set on one that has. Same bytes, different verdict. Trace, 4 equal-stake validators {A,B,C,D}, A slashed (or leaves) in block(R): post-change set {B,C,D}, quorum >2/3 of 3 requires all three. A's vertex V at R+2 (valid parents) reaches C and D before they execute block(R): admitted; C_{R+3}, D_{R+3} cite V. B executes block(R) first, then receives V: validator_set_at(R+2) = {B,C,D} -> REJECTED at ingress (design §3.2) and dropped (no park, no fetch in Part I). B's resolve_walk(C_{R+3}) -> V absent -> Unresolved{V}; V is never admitted on B (rejected again on every redelivery), so the release hook (a) never fires. B at R+4 can cite only B_{R+3} -> R4 fails -> B never proposes again. C_{R+4}, D_{R+4} cite [B,C,D]_{R+3}; every later vertex descends through V -> unresolvable on B forever. Anchor R+4 needs R+5 votes from all of B,C,D -> no direct commit ever -> no block -> no ChainSync -> no adopt_synced_anchor rescue. Permanent halt with NO Byzantine actor (a voluntary leave_validator_set triggers it). Two more faces of the same defect: (i) the walk-edge check `parent.author ∈ validator_set_at(parent.round)` (§3) flips from valid to invalid on a node the moment the row lands, and `Resolved` is 'authoritative until pruned' only in an in-memory cache — a node that restarts (or first walks) after block(R) evaluates the edge invalid while its peers already cited it; the design's sentence 'admitted everywhere, resolves nowhere — deterministic' is false because 'invalid' is a function of whether block(R) has executed locally; (ii) JOIN is worse: a joining validator N's account object is created by executing its first tx (executor:3029-3050), so a node that has not executed that block hits resolve_author_pubkey -> None -> silent `return` (dag.rs:995-1000) before membership is even consulted — a local-state ingress gate the design does not list among the '12 checks'. Off-by-one even at the boundary: block(R)'s own cone contains the offender's round-R vertex and its R+1 citers, so 'effect at anchor round R' invalidates edges inside the sequence that was just committed.
which_invariant: I1 (a hole from an admitted vertex must never reach the commit path — here honest citers become permanent holes on late nodes); I6 (admission not identical across nodes); I10 (a node that executed one block earlier than its peers can never re-enter); v2 #5 (admission as a function of local state) is reintroduced, not fixed
design_section: §3 (edge checks inside the walk, 'resolves nowhere — deterministic'), §3.2 (validator_set_at, 'written where sys:validator_set:v1 is written today'), §3.3 ('Ingress keeps only what is a pure function of bytes'), §12 ('R4 stops a lagging node ... intended'). Code: dag.rs:995-1000, :1077-1088; executor/src/lib.rs:1675-1680, :1732, :2532-2590, :3456-3475; ordering.rs:558-567, :663-686
design_fix: (1) Define the effect round as a pure function that is strictly above anything in flight: a change executed in block(anchor R) takes effect at round R + D with D a protocol constant (e.g. 64) ≥ the maximum commit-to-proposal lag; rows are keyed `sys:validator_set_at:{R+D}`. (2) For r beyond the highest DETERMINED round (latest_block_round + D), validator_set_at(r) must return Undetermined, never the current set. (3) Membership and pubkey resolution must then never be ingress rejections at all in Part I: admit any author present in (current set ∪ every retained snapshot ∪ authors of retained snapshots' rounds), and make the walk-edge check three-valued — Valid / Invalid / Deferred{until: latest_block_round ≥ parent.round − D}; Deferred is an Unresolved verdict with a synthetic blocked_on key `vset@round` released from the block-execution hook (the same place the row is written), so the verdict converges on every node to the same value once the block executes. (4) The pubkey gate must accept the vertex's own carried public key (verify sig against it and derive_address == author) when no account object exists yet, so joins are admitted before the join block executes. (5) Add the missing test row: slash/leave in block(R) while A keeps emitting at R+1..R+3; assert every node admits those bytes and cites identically; mutation = 'effect at R'. Row 8 as written (round < slash round) cannot detect this.

title: Timestamp future-drift check is a node-local hard DROP, not the 'deferral' §12 claims; a 29 s-future vertex splits honest admission by clock skew and, post-slash with 3 active validators, stalls the chain for every round the attacker chooses
attack: dag.rs:980-991: `if vertex.timestamp > now + 30 { return; }` — `now` is the receiver's wall clock; the vertex is discarded before dedup, not parked. §3.3 lists this among the '12 checks' that are 'a pure function of bytes' and §12 says 'deferral, retried' — both false at HEAD. Attack (needs a validator key, same threat model as the B3/B4 wedge Part I claims to close): A emits V_r with timestamp = now_A + 29 s and valid parents. Honest B whose clock is ≥ now_A − 1 s admits V_r; C and D whose clocks are ≥ 1 s behind A reject it (ordinary NTP spread). B_{r+1} cites [A,B,C,D]_r and resolves fine on B. On C: resolve_walk(B_{r+1}) -> V_r absent -> Unresolved{V_r}; nothing will re-deliver V_r: gossipsub's message-id cache suppresses the identical bytes for 60 s (p2p.rs:119-123), and the only re-push is the below-quorum loop (dag.rs:881-926) which sends dag.values() of a STUCK node — C and D do not hold V_r. C, D at r+2 can cite only [C,D]_{r+1} -> 2/4 not > 2/3 -> they do not propose (R4, §3.1). B at r+3 sees only A_{r+2}, B_{r+2} -> B stops too. All honest proposing stops until B itself falls below quorum and re-pushes V_r (round window ≥ current−3) AND the 60 s dedup on C/D has expired — a multi-round stall per attacker vertex, repeatable every round A is entitled to propose, so sustained throughput collapses to roughly one round per dedup window. After the set shrinks to 3 active validators (post-slash), quorum needs all three: one rejecting node is enough to freeze proposals entirely until the re-push lands. The design's I1 argument in §3.4 ('every honest vertex cites > 2/3 so the skip premise holds') silently assumes honest nodes agree on what was admitted; this check guarantees they do not.
which_invariant: I1 / I6 (same bytes admitted on one honest node and rejected on another through a receiver-clock predicate); I2 (the dropped vertex is unobtainable in Part I — only a below-quorum node pushes, and it is the node that lacks it); v2 #5 class (admission as a function of local state)
design_section: §3.3 ('the existing 12 checks' as pure functions of bytes), §12 ('Timestamp future-drift is node-local; deferral, retried'), §3.4. Code: dag.rs:980-991 (hard return), :881-926 (re-push only from below-quorum holders), :1884-1920 (broadcast paths), core/node/src/p2p.rs:119-123 (60 s duplicate cache keyed on sha256 of payload)
design_fix: Remove the wall-clock predicate from ingress. Either (a) bound the timestamp against a deterministic quantity every node agrees on — the BFT block time of the latest committed block (blockchain::bft_block_timestamp, already used for headers) plus a fixed protocol slack, which is a pure function of the committed chain — or (b) keep the wall-clock bound but express it as a walk-edge Deferred verdict (Unresolved{blocked_on: time@ts}) with the body ADMITTED and held in dag, released by the tick re-walk once local `now` passes ts − 30 s; the vertex is then cited by everyone or by no one at the same logical point. In both cases the design must state that no ingress `return` may depend on the receiver's clock, and add a test row: A emits ts = now+29 s, receivers skewed ±2 s; assert identical citation sets and no proposer stall; mutation = restore the ingress drop.

title: The executor cannot key `sys:validator_set_at:{round}` because it never receives the anchor round; the build path and the sync path would derive different keys for the same block, and if the row sits under the block write log the state roots diverge
attack: §3.2 says the row is 'written where sys:validator_set:v1 is written today' and 'keyed by the anchor round at which it took effect'. Every v1 writer is inside the executor (slash: executor:2532-2590 via logged_put at step 0, :1732; join/leave: :3456-3475 staged into `updates`), and the executor's entry point is execute_block_parallel_at(txs, proposer, block_height, evidence) (:1675-1680) — no round. On the local build path the block does not exist yet when the executor runs (dag.rs:1504 executes first, Block::new_with_roots_at at :1600-1620 afterwards), so the only round the executor can read from storage is the PREVIOUS block's header.round / `latest_block_round`. On the ChainSync path (sync/src/lib.rs:1076-1085) the block is in hand and block.header.round is the correct anchor round. An implementation that derives the key from storage therefore writes `validator_set_at:{R_prev}` on the node that built the block and `validator_set_at:{R}` on every node that synced it. Because v1's writers are under the write log (state_root folds every post-loop write, :2031-2040 comment), the row lands in the state root -> builder and syncers compute different state_root for the same block -> sync rejects the block as a fork (the BlockExecOutcome::AlreadyExecuted 'FORK' branch at sync:1090-1110). If instead the row is kept out of the write log, the rows silently disagree per node and every validator_set_at(r) lookup near the boundary is node-dependent — the §3.2 determinism premise fails by construction. Either way the anchor round is a required input the design does not plumb.
which_invariant: I6 (row availability/identity must be identical on validator, syncing, and observer nodes); state-root determinism (audit-B4b class: height-vs-round mapping must be a pure function of the block)
design_section: §3.2 ('written where sys:validator_set:v1 is written today ... keyed by the anchor round'), §4 (new state rows). Code: executor/src/lib.rs:1675-1680 (signature has no round), :1732, :2532-2590, :3456-3475; dag.rs:1504-1512 (execute before block construction), :1600-1620 (round assigned after); sync/src/lib.rs:1076-1085
design_fix: Add `anchor_round: u64` to execute_block_parallel_at and pass commit.anchor_round on the build path (dag.rs:1504) and block.header.round on the sync path (sync:1076); validate_block must already bind header.round into the signed header hash so a peer cannot supply a different round for the same height. Key the row on anchor_round + D (see the CRITICAL finding) and write it in the same logged batch as v1 so it is covered by the state root on both paths identically. State explicitly in §3.2 that the row is part of the state root and that the executor never infers the round from storage.

title: R4′ 'defer, never skip' on a resolved sub-quorum leader vertex pins the cursor forever — one Byzantine leader halts the chain with a fully valid 1-parent vertex
attack: Validator X is leader_for_round(r) for an even r (ordering.rs:916-960). X emits V_r with parents = [H_{r-1}] — one honest round-(r-1) vertex, exact round, author in set. Every ingress check passes (dag.rs:1000-1187). R1 asks only that every path from V_r terminates in genesis/committed through held bodies; it does (via H). So resolve_walk(V_r) = Resolved on every honest node. R4 (§3.1) constrains only the PROPOSER'S OWN cited set, not the parent count of a cited vertex, so every honest round-(r+1) proposer cites V_r alongside the other resolved round-r vertices. direct_quorum_met(r, V_r) (ordering.rs:650-671) is therefore true on every node; step 1 (ordering.rs:558-567) selects r as the smallest direct anchor. §3.3 then declares V_r not anchor-eligible (present parent stake 1/4 ≤ 2/3) and says the node 'defers (returns empty); it is never skipped by proof'. Nothing can change: V_r's parents are fixed bytes, so eligibility never becomes true; next_anchor_round stays at r; every subsequent try_commit re-selects r and returns empty. No anchor ≥ r ever commits on any node; blocks stop; sync cannot heal it because no node builds a block past r. X repeats this every even round it leads. If the implementer instead makes step 1 scan past the ineligible round, step 2 (ordering.rs:583-597) walks back from r+2, finds V_r ∈ visited (honest r+1 vertices cite it) and hits `Some(hj) if visited.contains(&hj)` — either committing at the ineligible vertex (violating R4′) or, applying §3.3 'as a chain link', deferring again = same halt. Test row 5 asserts 'skipped identically within 2 anchors', directly contradicting §3.3's 'never skipped'; the implementation will be bent to make row 5 green while the spec text produces a halt — the same pattern as the three shipped tests. No fake hash, no equivocation, no fetch needed.
which_invariant: I1 — the commit path must never wedge on an admitted vertex; also the design's own §0/§3.4 claim that Part I 'closes the malicious wedge … no buffer, no fetch, no state'.
design_fix: Replace deferral with a deterministic SKIP for a leader vertex that is resolved (walk complete) but sub-quorum: in step 1 treat it as 'no direct anchor at r' and continue scanning; in step 2 treat it as 'not in visited' (skip j). This is sound because eligibility is computed over a COMPLETE walk on identical bytes (present == cited), so every node reaches the same verdict, and R4′'s purpose (a thin vertex can never be the proving chain) is preserved. Rewrite §3.3 to say exactly that, delete 'never skipped by proof', and make row 5's mutation 'treat sub-quorum as eligible' plus a second row whose mutation is 'defer instead of skip' (assert the cursor passes r within 2 anchors on all nodes). Specify that only parents passing the edge check (round-1, member of validator_set_at) count toward eligibility.

title: validator_set_at(vertex.round) is undefined for rounds above the local execution tip; the node-local fill-in makes admission admit-here/reject-there, and the admitting honest node is silently excluded from citation for good
attack: Set changes are written by the executor while executing the block of anchor k (executor/src/lib.rs:866-912 leave; :2532-2580 slash). Anchor k needs round-(k+1) votes (ordering.rs:558-567, :650-671), so block k executes when the DAG is already at round ≥ k+2, and execution timing differs per node (any routine hole defers a node, ordering.rs:731-737; dag.rs:1306-1310). Honest departing validator X (leave tx in block k; X's own node has not executed k yet) has already gossiped X_{k+2}. Node N1 executes block k, then receives X_{k+2}: §3.2 says ingress uses validator_set_at(k+2); the only snapshot key ≤ k+2 is k (X removed) → REJECT at the dag.rs:1082 check; the body is dropped and Part I has no fetch. Node N4 (deferred on a hole, executes k a few rounds later) receives X_{k+2} first → its latest snapshot is k-2 (X present) → ADMIT. N4's resolve_walk(X_{k+2}) = Resolved; N4 cites it in N4_{k+3} (§3.1) and, because try_create_vertex cites round_index[prev] including its own previous vertex (dag.rs:529-536) and a Resolved cache entry is 'authoritative until the vertex is pruned' (§3), every later N4 vertex transitively cites X_{k+2}. On N1..N3 resolve_walk(N4_{k+3}) reaches X_{k+2} ∉ dag, ∉ committed_set (it is only in N4's cone, which is never cited, so it never enters committed_set via sync) → Unresolved forever. N4 is never cited again until it restarts (cold cache re-walk hits the pruned hole). With n=4 the chain now needs all 3 remaining vertices every round; N4's payloads never execute, N4 earns nothing. §3 claims 'admission must be a pure function of the vertex bytes plus state identical on every node' and §3.2 claims v2 #6/#9 closed — both false: the snapshot lookup for any round above the local executed anchor is local state. (At HEAD the same race wedges commit instead — Part I is better than HEAD here, but the claim is wrong and the burn-in cannot see the exclusion, see the next hole.)
which_invariant: v2 #5 property restated in §3 (admission = pure function of bytes + identical state); I9-class 'citable-but-unobtainable hash' (I2: no pull exists in Part I to repair it).
design_fix: Define validator_set_at(round) explicitly for round > highest snapshot key, and make it sender-independent by giving set changes an ACTIVATION ROUND that no gossiped vertex can precede: a change executed at anchor k takes effect for vertices at round ≥ k + D where D is fixed and larger than the DAG's lead over execution (bound the lead: ingress already caps round ≤ current+10_000, so either cap the lead to a small D at ingress for membership purposes, or activate at the next epoch boundary, which the executor already snapshots as sys:validator_set:epoch:{E}, executor:1306-1309, and which QC verification already uses). Vertices at rounds in [k, k+D) are checked against the pre-change set on every node. Add a test whose mutation is 'apply the set change immediately at anchor k' and whose assertion is that a departing validator's vertices at k+1..k+D-1 are admitted on a node that executed k before receiving them AND cited identically on all nodes.

title: The Stage 1 burn-in criterion is vacuously satisfiable: ChainSync copies blocks byte-for-byte, no RPC distinguishes a locally built block from an adopted one, and per-validator inclusion is not measured — silent exclusion and a wedged local commit path both pass
attack: §4's criterion is 'byte-identical committed sequences and identical anchor_hash per height on every node'. The only per-height RPC surface at HEAD is GET /get_block?height=N (api_local.rs:2119-2148), which returns the stored block_{h} JSON, and aincore_getFinalityStatus (api_local.rs:903-920), which exposes only last_anchor_round/hash/digest. ChainSync process_blocks (sync/src/lib.rs:928-1010) persists the PEER's block verbatim under block_{h}; reload_chain_tip then calls adopt_synced_anchor with block.committed_vertices verbatim (dag.rs:2852-2884; ordering.rs:869-888), and the local build for that anchor is skipped when anchor_round ≤ latest_block_round (dag.rs:1306-1310). Consequence 1: a node whose local commit path is permanently wedged (hole #1, or any R1 bug) but whose ChainSync works shows blocks identical to the producer's — criterion green while Part I's core mechanism never ran on 3 of 4 nodes. Consequence 2 (the v1 failure the criterion claims to catch): if validator N4's vertices are never cited (hole #2, or any verdict asymmetry), they are in no anchor's cone, so every node — including N4, which commits the same cones locally — produces identical committed_vertices that simply omit N4. 48 h of identical blocks, zero stall, N4 excluded the whole time. The criterion measures cross-node AGREEMENT; silent exclusion is an agreement failure between the DAG and the sequence, which agreement cannot see. Nothing at HEAD records 'built locally' vs 'adopted' per height, and nothing reports per-author citation or inclusion coverage.
which_invariant: §4 exit criterion; makes I1 and the v2 #5 determinism claim unverifiable in Part I's gate (I6-class: a signal that does not mean what the gate assumes).
design_section: §4 exit criterion, §10 'live' row; api_local.rs:2119-2148, :903-920; sync/src/lib.rs:928-1010; dag.rs:1306-1310, :2852-2884
design_fix: Add to Part I two observable, RPC-exposed signals and put both in the exit criterion: (1) per height, an origin marker (locally_committed | adopted_from_sync) plus the local try_commit decision log (anchor round → commit/skip/defer with the leader hash), and require that every validator's LOCAL decision sequence is identical across nodes and that ≥ X % of heights on every node are locally committed; (2) per round, per author, whether that author's vertex was (a) admitted, (b) Resolved, (c) cited by ≥ 2/3 stake at r+1, (d) present in some block's committed_vertices within k anchors — and require 100 % of honest authors reach (d) for every round of the burn-in. Reject the burn-in if any validator's citation rate at r+1 drops below 2/3 for more than a handful of consecutive rounds.

title: Part I leaves the audit-119 equivocation wedge (I9) as a one-key permanent halt while §0 claims Part I 'closes the malicious wedge' and is shippable alone; R4 turns the asymmetric split into a symmetric proposal halt
attack: n = 4 (X attacker, N1, N2, N3). X sends twin A_r to N1 and twin B_r to N2, N3 (direct TCP to chosen peers, or just gossip race). At ingress the second-arriving twin on each node is dropped without insertion and every redelivery is dropped again (dag.rs:1139-1170: equivocation branch returns before persist/insert) — unchanged by Part I. Round r+1: N1's resolved round-r candidates are [A, N1_r, N2_r, N3_r] → cites all (4/4); N2, N3 cite [B, …]. Round r+2: on N1, N2_{r+1} and N3_{r+1} cite B ∉ dag, ∉ committed_set → Unresolved; N1's cited stake = {N1, X} = 2/4 → R4 fails → no proposal. On N2/N3, N1_{r+1} cites A → Unresolved → cited stake {N2, N3} = 2/4 → R4 fails. All honest proposers stop; re-gossip (dag.rs:881-926) redelivers A to N2 which drops it as equivocation again. No anchor ever commits (there is no block for sync to adopt); apply_equivocation_slash writes only local rows (validator:jailed / sys:equiv_seen), never sys:validator_set:v1 (executor-only), so X's stake stays in the denominator. Permanent halt, no fetch could help even if it existed because the twin is rejected at ingress. At HEAD the same key wedges commit_one_anchor instead (I9) — Part I neither worsens nor closes it, yet §0 says Part I 'closes the malicious wedge' and §11 gates Stage 1 shipping on Part I alone. Part I is shippable only as 'closes the fake-parent wedge; equivocation halt still one key away'.
which_invariant: I9 — equivocation must never create a citable-but-unobtainable hash; §0/§3.4 claim of closure.
design_fix: Either (a) move the minimal shadow store (§6: one compact+parents row per (author, round), loaded at boot, read by resolve_walk over dag ∪ shadow, never in round_index) into Part I so a citation of either twin resolves once both are held — this needs no messages, only a second ingress path for the counterpart body; or (b) state in §0/§11 that Part I does NOT close B3/B4 and cannot ship as the closure, and put the I9 test (twins split 2:2 and 3:1 with Part I only; assert the chain keeps committing) into Part I's gate. Either way add the row with mutation 'drop the second twin at ingress'.

title: A parent in committed_set with an absent body bypasses the edge check, so the same bytes resolve on one node and not another; R4′'s 'present parent bodies' count then diverges and one side commits while the other defers
attack: walk_history treats h ∉ dag as settled iff h == 'genesis' or h ∈ committed_set (ordering.rs:697-702) BEFORE any body is inspected; sync adoption puts hashes into committed_set with no body (ordering.rs:869-888 via dag.rs:2852-2884; the design's own S2 'body may be absent'). §3's edge check needs parent.round and parent.author, which come only from the body. Attack: X (leader of even round r) emits V_r with parents = [P, H1_{r-1}, H2_{r-1}] where P is a REAL vertex at round r-5 by author A, already committed everywhere. Node N1 still holds P's body (prune horizon is finalized-10, dag.rs:1786-1808) → edge P has round r-5 ≠ r-1 → V_r Unresolved → not cited. Node N2 lost P in transit (routine 5 % loss, the live row's own parameter) and settled it via sync → walk reaches P ∈ committed_set → settled, edge never evaluated → V_r Resolved → N2 cites it. §3's 'admitted everywhere and resolves nowhere — deterministic' is false, and row 6 (all nodes hold all bodies) cannot observe it. Then R4′: V_r ∈ visited on all nodes (through N2_{r+1}); on N1 present parent bodies = {A, H1, H2} = 3/4 (design does not say wrong-round parents are excluded) → eligible → step 2 commits r at V_r; on N2, P absent → 2/4 → ineligible → defer (hole #1 semantics) → N2's local cursor is stuck at r until it adopts N1's block. Node-local eligibility is exactly the v2 #5 class relocated from ingress to the commit path.
which_invariant: §3 determinism property (v2 #5); I1 on the deferring node.
design_fix: Make the settled-without-body case carry what the edge check needs: record (hash, round, author) for every committed vertex (extend Block.committed_vertices / cseq rows, or a parallel committed_meta map bounded with committed_set) so the walk can evaluate round-1 and membership for a bodiless settled parent identically on every node. Define R4′ to count only parents that pass the edge check. Add a row whose fixture has one node with P bodiless-but-settled and whose mutation is 'skip the edge check for committed parents', asserting identical citation and identical anchor eligibility on both nodes.

title: Part I's gate is internally inconsistent and two of its rows pass by harness injection of a delivery Part I cannot perform — row 8 needs a fetched body (Part II) and row 3's 'redelivery' does not exist in Part I
attack: §4 says the exit is rows 1–7; §11 Stage 1 says rows 1–8. Row 8 (slashed_author_body_still_admissible_at_its_round) is defined on 'a fetched body' — fetch is §5 (Stage 2–3). In Part I the only way to run it is to call add_vertex directly, which tests the validator_set_at lookup in isolation while the live path's lookup for rounds above the tip is undefined (hole #2). Row 3 (sub_quorum_cited_parents_do_not_propose) asserts 'peers and it converge after redelivery'. In Part I the only redelivery is the below-quorum re-gossip push (dag.rs:881-926); in the row's own fixture the lacking node is 1 of 4, so the three holders stay above quorum and never push, and gossipsub drops a byte-identical re-publish for 60 s anyway (p2p.rs:119-123). The node converges only when ChainSync adopts a block containing the missing vertex (settled without body, dag.rs:2852-2884) — so Part I's liveness after any single loss is secretly dependent on block sync, which the design never states, and the row is satisfiable by the harness handing the vertex to add_vertex regardless of whether the live path could obtain it. Both rows can be green with the live mechanism absent.
which_invariant: I2 (redelivery must be a pull from a holder — Part I has none, and its test pretends otherwise); gate consistency between §4 and §11.
design_section: §4 exit criterion, §10 rows 3 and 8, §11 Stage 1 gate; dag.rs:881-926, :2852-2884; p2p.rs:119-123
design_fix: Make §4 and §11 agree on the row set. Move row 8 to Part II or rewrite it for Part I as 'late-gossip body from a since-removed author, at its own round, arriving after the removing block executed, admitted on a node that executed that block' with the mutation 'use the current set'. Rewrite row 3 so the convergence step is the ONLY mechanism Part I actually has — ChainSync adoption of a block carrying the missing vertex, with gossip fully disabled and no direct add_vertex injection — and state in §12 that Part I's recovery from any single-vertex loss depends on block sync. Add a row whose fixture disables ChainSync and asserts the stall is bounded, or document that it is not.

title: Decision rule is selected by local twin knowledge: untwinned nodes decide r by ancestry, twin-aware nodes by E2, and the two rules disagree
attack: n=4 equal stake, honest H1,H2,H3, Byzantine X = leader(r). X builds twins A,B at r. X delivers A to H1 early; delays A to H2 and H3 until after each has proposed its r+1 vertex (H2,H3 cite {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r} = 3/4 > 2/3, so R4 lets them propose without any twin); then X sends A followed by B to H3 only (direct TCP, `send_message`). State: H1 holds A (dag) and cited A at r+1; H2 holds A only; H3 holds A (dag) + B (shadow, S4). Round-(r+1) votes everywhere: H1→A, H2→∅, H3→∅, X→∅ or absent. Round r+2 leader is honest and its vertex cites {H1_{r+1},H2_{r+1},H3_{r+1}}; r+3 votes give it a direct commit. Step 2 now decides r on each node: H1 and H2 have `leader_vertex_hash(r) = {A}` (untwinned) so, per §6 last bullet 'for an untwinned leader, step 2 is unchanged', they use `visited`: H1_{r+1} ∈ visited and it cites A, so A ∈ visited → COMMIT r at A (ordering.rs:583-597). H3 has twins {A,B} so it must use E2: walked r+1 set = 4/4 ≥ 2/3, Σ votes = 1/4 ≤ 1/3 → SKIP r. H1/H2 build height h from anchor A (round r); H3 builds height h from round r+2 — the B4b block fork. Nothing ever repairs it: nobody cites B, so H1/H2 never WANTED it; EQUIV_PROOF gossip from H3 cannot create a shadow on H1/H2 because §10 `phantom_proof_does_not_change_anchors` requires proofs not to change decisions (and if proofs DID create shadows, that test fails instead — the design is caught both ways). The same fork also occurs with no delivery trick at all whenever one node decides r before the second twin reaches it and another decides after. This is exactly the v2 root-cause class: §6 claims the decision 'never depends on which twin arrived first' but it depends on WHETHER a twin has arrived at decision time. The consistency argument in §6 ('a node that already committed r directly at t … every node that later learns of the twin still reaches commit at t') covers only DIRECT commits; it says nothing about the far more common ancestry commit, and that is where it breaks.
which_invariant: I9 (equivocation must never make the decision node-local); v2 root cause (decision depends on local twin arrival)
design_section: §6 E2 bullet 4 ('Step 2 never decides a twinned round by visited … For an untwinned leader, step 2 is unchanged') and the consistency paragraph after E2; code ordering.rs:583-597 (step-2 visited decision), :634-647 (leader_vertex_hash), dag.rs:1143-1168 (equivocation branch)
design_fix: There must be ONE decision function for every leader round, evaluated identically whether or not the node knows of a twin. Adopt Mysticeti's uncertified-DAG rule (research A: 'support' rule) in place of E2 + the untwinned/twinned split: (1) each round-(r+1) vertex SUPPORTS exactly one vertex per (author, round) — the first twin reached in a deterministic order over its parent list — so a vertex citing both twins still supports one; (2) DIRECT commit of t requires a certificate pattern visible in the cone: > 2/3 stake of round-(r+2) vertices each of whose parents include > 2/3 stake of round-(r+1) supporters of t; (3) DIRECT skip requires > 2/3 stake of round-(r+1) vertices that do not support t (blame); (4) otherwise decide INDIRECTLY from the lowest later committed anchor: commit t iff that anchor's cone contains a certificate for t, else skip. Because certificates and blames are cone-visible, a node that never sees the twin and a node that holds both evaluate the same predicate on the same cone. Delete the sentence 'for an untwinned leader, step 2 is unchanged' and re-run the §10 A3_B1/A2_B2 tests with the twin delivered to ONE node only and to NO node until after one node has decided r.

title: E2's middle band (1/3 < Σ votes, no twin > 2/3) is undecidable with complete information: one equivocating leader halts the chain forever
attack: n=4 equal stake, X = leader(r) sends A to H1,H2 and B to H3 (each first), then the counterpart to everyone, so every honest node holds both twins (dag + shadow). Round-(r+1) votes: H1→A, H2→A, H3→B, X→∅ (X cites only {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r}, which is a legal 3/4 parent set) or X sends nothing. Every honest node holds all four r+1 bodies. E2 on every node: votes(A)=2/4 (not > 2/3), votes(B)=1/4, Σ=3/4 > 1/3 → neither commit nor skip → 'defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes' — but no vote is missing; every author's r+1 body is held. Step 1 scans past r to a later direct anchor r_direct; step 2 reaches j=r and, per §6, may not decide it by `visited`, so it returns `out` empty (ordering.rs:583-597 pattern); the cursor never advances (only apply_anchor_bookkeeping advances it, ordering.rs:776). No node ever produces a block ≥ r, so ChainSync/adopt_synced_anchor (dag.rs:2852-2884) has nothing to adopt. Total, permanent liveness failure from a single validator key, cheaper than HEAD's wedge (no fake parent needed). At n=7 the same holds with a 3:2 honest split and X,Y silent at r+1 (max twin votes 3/7 < 5/7 required, Σ=5/7 > 1/3). Bullshark closes this band by ancestry from the next anchor; v3 removed that path for twinned rounds and supplied no replacement.
which_invariant: I1 (the commit path must never encounter an undecidable state from an admitted vertex) — liveness form; Part I exit criterion 'never wedge or fork' (§12)
design_section: §6 E2 bullet 3 ('Otherwise defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes') together with bullet 4; §7 row 2 ('or defers and fetches votes'); code ordering.rs:558-567 (step 1 scan), :583-597 (step 2 early return), :776 (cursor advance)
design_fix: A leader round must always be decidable once the next anchor is committed: replace defer-forever with the indirect rule from hole 1 (decide r from the lowest later committed anchor's cone — commit t iff the cone certifies t, else skip). Deferral is only permitted while the cone is INCOMPLETE (a genuine hole), never while it is complete. Add a test `twinned_round_split_2_1_offender_silent_is_decided_within_two_anchors` whose mutation is 'keep E2's defer branch'.

title: E2's skip rule is not intersection-sound: a > 2/3 direct commit and a '≥ 2/3 walked, ≤ 1/3 Σ' skip coexist when the offender also twins its r+1 vote
attack: n=4 equal stake. X = leader(r), twins A (to H1,H2 first) and B (to H3 first); all nodes eventually hold both. Round-(r+1): H1→A, H2→A, H3→∅ (H3 proposed before any twin arrived, citing {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r}). X equivocates AGAIN at r+1 (free — it is already 100 % slashed for r): X1 cites A, delivered to H1 only; X2 cites ∅, delivered to H2,H3. Gossip delays H2_{r+1} to H3 (ordinary 5 % loss, §10 live row) or X simply never relays it. H1: held r+1 = {H1(A),H2(A),H3(∅),X1(A)} → votes(A)=3/4 > 2/3 → direct COMMIT r at A (`direct_quorum_met` counts every held body, ordering.rs:650-676). H3: held r+1 = {H1(A),H3(∅),X2(∅)} = 3/4 ≥ 2/3 walked, Σ votes = 1/4 ≤ 1/3 → SKIP r. The §6 justification ('quorum intersection proves no direct quorum for any twin ever existed') is false: the > 2/3 quorum and the ≥ 2/3 walked set intersect in ≥ 2 authors, but one of them is X whose r+1 body differs per node, leaving only 1/4 honest stake in the intersection. In general the honest part of the intersection is > 1/3 − f, which is ≤ 1/3 for any f > 0. Same at n=7 (f=2): A direct with {H1,H2,H3,X1,Y1} = 5/7; a node holding {H1(A),H4(B),H5(B),X2(∅),Y2(∅)} has 5/7 walked and Σ=3/7… so make H4,H5 cite ∅ instead of B: Σ=1/7 ≤ 1/3 → skip while H-side committed A. H1 builds height h at anchor A; H3 builds height h from r+2: block-level fork.
which_invariant: I9 (no node-local decision under equivocation); §6's own 'at most one twin can pass, by quorum intersection'
design_section: §6 E2 bullet 2 ('If the walked round-(r+1) set held ≥ 2/3 stake and Σ votes ≤ 1/3: skip … quorum intersection proves …'); code ordering.rs:650-676 (direct_quorum_met over all held r+1 bodies), dag.rs:1143-1168 (second r+1 twin goes to shadow, still 'held')
design_fix: A skip proof must be a cone-visible blame: > 2/3 stake of round-(r+1) vertices that each do NOT support t, where each author contributes at most one r+1 vertex chosen deterministically (the one in the deciding anchor's cone), never 'whatever this node happens to hold'. Direct commit likewise must be a cone-visible certificate (hole 1). With both keyed on the same cone, a commit certificate and a skip blame for the same (author, round) cannot both exist under f < 1/3 (they intersect in > 1/3 stake, and a single deterministically chosen r+1 vertex per author cannot both support and blame t). Add test `direct_commit_vs_skip_with_r1_twin` asserting identical anchor_hash on all nodes; mutation: 'count held bodies instead of cone bodies'.

title: The winning twin can be this node's SHADOW: block build and find_causal_history read only `dag`, so the committed block has no payload for it and the sequence order differs per node
attack: n=4. X = leader(r) sends A first to H1,H2 and B first to H3; the counterpart follows. H3 holds B in dag/round_index and A in shadow (compact + parents, no payload). Votes: H1→A, H2→A, H3→B, X→A (X's single r+1 vertex). votes(A)=3/4 → E2 commits r at A on EVERY node (this is the design's happy path, §7 row 2). On H3, `commit_one_anchor(A)`: `find_causal_history` (ordering.rs:964-1010) does `dag.get(&hash)` at :975 — A is not in `dag`, so A itself is not pushed into `history` and its parents are not traversed (a parent P cited only by A is silently omitted); the sort at :1002 puts any hash not in `dag` last. So H3's committed sequence (a) omits A's exclusive ancestry, (b) orders A's cone differently from H1/H2, and the finality digest diverges. Even if find_causal_history is changed to read dag ∪ shadow, the block-build loop (dag.rs:1345-1383) does `dag.get(hash)` per sequence hash: for A it hits the else-branch, prints COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING and drops A's transactions from `block_txs` — and the shadow has no payload to supply anyway (compact form strips it, blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461). H1/H2 execute A's transactions; H3 does not → different state root, different block hash at the same height. Symmetrically, when both twins are in the cone (H3's r+1 vertex cites B), H1/H2 lack B's payload and H3 lacks A's: every node executes a different transaction set for height h. §6 'the sequence orders whatever the cone contains' is therefore a fork, not a determinism argument. Note the shadow is arrival-defined ('the first counterpart'): which twin is compact is exactly the arrival-order dependence v3 set out to remove.
which_invariant: I9; Part I/II exit criterion 'byte-identical committed sequences and identical anchor_hash per height'
design_section: §6 'Shadow storage' (compact form plus parents; 'the walk needs parents, not payload') and E1 (anchor may be a shadow); §6 'No exclusion rule … the sequence orders whatever the cone contains'; code ordering.rs:975, :1002; dag.rs:1345-1383; blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461
design_fix: Any vertex that can be an anchor or appear in a committed sequence must be held in LIVE form with payload on every node, and every consumer must read one store. Simplest sound option (research C:121 option (a)): admit BOTH twins into `dag`/`round_index` as live vertices (they are hash-bound and signed), drop the shadow tier entirely, keep the slash via evidence, and bound per-author bytes per round window (I4/I11) instead of per-(author, round) count. If a shadow tier is kept, it must store the full live body and `walk_history`, `find_causal_history`, the sort key, and dag.rs:1346 must all read dag ∪ shadow, with an explicit test `winning_twin_held_as_shadow_executes_same_block` (mutation: 'store shadow compact').

title: 'At most one shadow per (author, round)' recreates I9 for a third version: a citable twin that no node can ever obtain, wedging every node
attack: n=4. X = leader(r) or not (irrelevant). X signs three same-round vertices A, B, C. It delivers A first to H1, B first to H2, C first to H3, then all remaining versions to everyone. Under §6 each node keeps its first-arrived twin in dag and exactly ONE counterpart as shadow ('the first counterpart … any further same-round body from that author is dropped without writing', the `sys:equiv_seen` latch dag.rs:2287-2290): H1 holds {A,B}, drops C; H2 holds {B,C}, drops A; H3 holds {C,A}, drops B (X orders deliveries to make this so). Each honest node cites its own dag twin at r+1 (round_index). The honest leader of r+2 cites {H1,H2,H3}_{r+1} (3/4 > 2/3), so the anchor cone at r+2 contains A, B and C. On every node, `walk_history` (ordering.rs:697-712, or resolve_walk over dag ∪ shadow) hits the version it dropped → hole → `commit_one_anchor` returns None (ordering.rs:731-737). WANTED fires for the missing hash, the fetch reaches a peer that holds it, `VERTEX_RESP` delivers it, and the ingress latch drops it again without writing. No node ever commits r+2 or anything above; no block exists for adopt_synced_anchor to heal from. This is exactly the audit-119 I9 wedge, now requiring three signatures instead of two, and it is a direct consequence of the I4 bound chosen in §6.
which_invariant: I9 ('Equivocation must never create a citable-but-unobtainable hash')
design_section: §6 'Shadow storage' ('at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart … any further same-round body from that author is dropped without writing'); §9 row I4 ('shadow ≤ 1 per (author, round)'); code dag.rs:2287-2290 (latch), ordering.rs:697-712 (walk hole), :731-737
design_fix: The bound must be on what honest nodes can CITE, not on count: an honest round-(r+1) vertex cites at most one twin, so at most n distinct twins can ever be in any cone. Bound held versions per (author, round) by the validator count (or, better, admit all hash-distinct twins into `dag` and bound by bytes per author per window per I4/I11 — a few hundred bytes each if payload-stripped is acceptable for non-anchors, full body otherwise per hole 4). Add test `three_way_equivocation_does_not_wedge` (mutation: 'cap shadows at 1').

title: The compact+parents shadow form is not self-authenticating and cannot pass the single ingress gate: a serving peer forges the parent list and the walk verdict becomes node-local
attack: §6 stores and §5.3 serves the second twin as 'compact form plus parents' (`vertex_shadow:{H}`) and says every fetched body 'enters through handle_message — the single gate'. At HEAD there is no such form: `to_compact_proof` (blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461) sets `parents_root`/`payload_root` and EMPTIES both `payload` and `parents`. If parents are re-attached to a compact vertex, `calculate_hash` (lib.rs:520-543) folds `self.parents_root()` (lib.rs:429-434), which returns the explicit `parents_root` whenever it is `Some` and never compares it to the listed `parents`. So a malicious peer answering a Tier-A/Tier-B `VERTEX_REQ` for twin B returns B with the genuine hash, signature and roots but `parents = [Q]` where Q is a hash that will never exist: hash and signature verify, the shadow is stored, and every `resolve_walk`/`walk_history` through B on that node hits Q → Unresolved/hole, while a node that fetched B from an honest peer resolves it. Under Part II that makes the citer of B resolvable on some nodes and not others (R4 citations diverge per node), creates a WANTED[Q] that can never be satisfied, and — for a twinned anchor round — feeds E2 a cone that is complete on one node and holed on another (defer vs decide). Separately, the same body cannot enter through 'the single gate' as specified: `add_vertex` rejects any vertex with either root set at dag.rs:1036 ('live vertex … carries proof-only root fields'), so either a second gate exists (contradicting I6 / §5.3) or the shadow path is unspecified.
which_invariant: I6 (single admission gate; admitted iff inserted); I5 (idempotent per hash — same hash, different bodies per node)
design_section: §6 'Shadow storage' ('compact form plus parents'), §5.3 ('vertex:{H} or vertex_shadow:{H} … Each body enters through handle_message — the single gate'); code blockchain/src/lib.rs:429-434, :454-461, :520-543; dag.rs:1036
design_fix: Serve and store twins in live form (full `parents`, `payload`, no roots), so the existing hash recomputation at dag.rs:1062-1070 binds the parent list — this also resolves hole 4. If a compact-with-parents form is retained anywhere, the ingress for it must require `parents_root_of(vertex.parents) == vertex.parents_root` (and likewise for payload if present) before storing, and §5.3 must name the ingress branch that admits it, since dag.rs:1036 rejects it today. Add test `forged_shadow_parent_list_rejected` (mutation: 'skip the parents_root recomputation').

title: 'At most one twin can pass' silently assumes every honest r+1 vertex cites at most one twin, but §3.1 + §6 let the proposer's candidate list include the shadow
attack: §3.1 says `try_create_vertex` 'cites only resolved round-(r−1) vertices' and §6 says `resolve_walk reads dag ∪ shadow`.
