At HEAD the candidate list is `round_index[prev]` verbatim (dag.rs:529-536) and the shadow is 'never in round_index', so today the list excludes the shadow — but Part II never states that the candidate list is `round_index` rather than 'everything resolved'. If an implementer takes §3.1 literally and cites every resolved round-(r−1) vertex, an honest node holding both twins cites both (uniqueness at dag.rs:1057 only forbids duplicate hashes). Then at n=4 with X = leader(r) delivering both twins to everyone before r+1: H1,H2,H3 each cite A AND B, votes(A)=votes(B)=3/4 or 4/4 — both > 2/3 — and E2 ('at most one twin can pass, by quorum intersection') has no tie-break, so the anchor for r is whichever twin the implementation iterates first: E1's 'ordered by hash' happens to make it deterministic only by accident, and step 3's `to_commit` takes the first found. Independently, the offender's own r+1 vertex citing both twins is legal today and counts its stake for both twins; that is safe under f < 1/3 only because the honest single-citation invariant holds — an invariant the design relies on for E2's soundness but never states or tests.
which_invariant: I9 (E2 determinism rests on an unstated citation invariant)
design_section: §3.1 R4 ('cites only resolved round-(r−1) vertices') read with §6 ('resolve_walk reads dag ∪ shadow'; 'at most one twin can pass, by quorum intersection'); code dag.rs:529-536, :1057
design_fix: State the invariant explicitly and make it structural: a vertex SUPPORTS at most one vertex per (author, round) regardless of how many it cites (Mysticeti support rule — first twin in a deterministic order over the parent list), and `votes(t)` counts support, not citation. State that the honest candidate list is `round_index[prev]` (never the shadow). Add test `r1_vertex_citing_both_twins_supports_one` (mutation: 'count citations instead of support').

title: E2 skip rule is not quorum-intersection-sound: one node commits round r at twin t while another skips r
attack: n=4 equal stake {H1,H2,H3,Z}. Z leads even round r and equivocates: t -> H1,H2 early; t' -> H3 only after H3 has already proposed r+1 (so H3 knows Z is a twin author but its r+1 body cites {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r}, 3/4 > 2/3 under R4, and votes for no twin). r+1 bodies: H1->t, H2->t, H3->none. Z equivocates again at r+1 (free, already slashable): z1 cites t, delivered to node A; z2 cites no twin, delivered to node B. Node A holds {H1,H2,z1}: votes(t)=3/4 > 2/3 -> E2 commits r at t. Node B holds {H2,H3,z2} = 3/4 >= 2/3 stake, sum of votes over all twins = H2 = 1/4 <= 1/3 -> E2 SKIPS r. try_commit runs on every add_vertex (dag.rs:1273-1295), so B decides on that snapshot before H1/z1 arrive, and skip is final. A's block at that height carries anchor r; B's does not: fork. The design's justification ('quorum intersection proves no direct quorum for any twin ever existed') fails because 2/3 ∩ 2/3 is only > 1/3 by author, and the Byzantine share of that intersection presents a different r+1 body to each node (z1 vs z2), leaving an honest overlap of 1/4 <= 1/3. Bullshark skips only when > 2/3 stake of r+1 bodies cite NO leader vertex; here the non-voters at B are {H3,z2} = 1/2, so Bullshark would defer. Second sequence via the one-shadow cap (§6): with three twins t,t',t'' a node that holds t and one shadow never learns t'' is Z's, so votes for t'' are not in sum_t votes(t) -> skip on that node, commit at t'' (> 2/3) on a node that holds t'' live. This is the same root cause class as v2 #2/#3/#4/#8/#10: the decision for an equivocating leader round still depends on which bodies arrived first.
which_invariant: I9 (equivocation must not change the anchor decision) / I1 determinism of the committed sequence
design_section: §6 Rule E2 ('If the walked round-(r+1) set held >= 2/3 stake and sum_t votes(t) <= 1/3: skip r'); §7 row 2; ordering.rs:558-567, 650-676; dag.rs:1273-1295
design_fix: Replace the skip predicate with Bullshark's: skip r iff the distinct-author stake of held round-(r+1) bodies that cite NO vertex by leader(r) at round r (over dag ∪ shadow, counting an author once even if it has r+1 twins) is > 2/3 of validator_set_at(r+1). Otherwise defer. Prove it: any direct commit at t needed > 2/3 voting t, which intersects any > 2/3 no-vote set in > 1/3 > f stake, and an honest author cannot be in both. Add test `leader_equivocation_A3_B1_with_r1_twin` reproducing the sequence above with the mutation 'held >= 2/3 and votes <= 1/3'.

title: Compact shadow (payload stripped) inside a committed cone: block content diverges between nodes that hold the twin live and nodes that hold it as shadow
attack: Non-leader Z at round r sends V (payload P1) to N1,N2 and V' (payload P2) to N3,N4. Each side cites its own twin at r+1 (both resolve locally). The anchor at r+2 cites both r+1 sides, so its cone contains V and V'. Per §5/§6 every node fetches the other twin and stores it as 'compact form plus parents' (§6: 'the walk needs parents, not payload'). §6 then says 'the sequence orders whatever the cone contains' (no exclusion rule). At block-build time dag.rs:1345-1385 reads `dag.get(hash)` for each hash in commit.sequence and pushes `v.payload` into block_txs; a shadow is 'never in round_index' and not in `dag`, so on N1 the loop either omits V' entirely (find_causal_history at ordering.rs:964-975 only pushes hashes with `dag.get(&hash).is_some()`, so V' is not even in N1's sequence, while it is in N3's) or hits the [COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING] branch whose own comment says 'block content will diverge'. N1 executes P1 only, N3 executes P2 only (and V' contributes a BFT-time sample on N3 but not N1, dag.rs:1375). Different committed_vertices, different txs, different state root, different block hash at the same height: fork with f=1. v2's exclusion rule was dropped because it was keyed on local state; v3 dropped the rule but kept the payload-less shadow, so the sequence is still node-local.
which_invariant: I9 / I1 (identical committed sequence and block on every node)
design_section: §6 'Shadow storage' (compact + parents) and 'No exclusion rule is needed'; §2 S4; dag.rs:1345-1385; ordering.rs:964-975; blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461
design_fix: Either (a) store the shadow as the FULL live body (payload included; it is bounded by MAX_VERTEX_BYTES and there is at most one per (author, round)) and make find_causal_history, the block builder's payload loop, and BFT-time sampling read dag ∪ shadow; or (b) keep compact shadows and add a deterministic exclusion keyed only on DAG-carried facts: a twin is excluded from the executed payload iff the other twin is also in the cone (both nodes then see the same pair and both drop both payloads while keeping the hashes in committed_vertices). Test: `equivocating_nonleader_in_cone_identical_block_hash` with 3:1 and 2:2 splits, asserting byte-identical block_txs and state root; mutation: strip payload from shadow.

title: One shadow per (author, round) turns a three-way equivocation into a permanent liveness halt with f=1
attack: n=4 {H1,H2,H3,Z}. Z signs three vertices V1,V2,V3 at round r and delivers exactly one to each honest node (V_i -> H_i), then produces nothing at r+1. Each H_i resolves and cites V_i at r+1 (plus the honest round-r vertices; 4/4 stake, R4 satisfied). At r+2 every H_i walks the other two r+1 vertices: H_j's cites V_j -> WANTED[V_j] -> fetched from H_j -> ingress: (Z, r) already has dag twin V_i; §6 stores 'at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart' and 'any further same-round body from that author is dropped without writing (the existing sys:equiv_seen latch, dag.rs:2287-2290)'. So H_i can store V_j but V_k is dropped forever; H_k's r+1 vertex is Unresolved on H_i forever. Citable r+1 stake on every honest node = 2/4 = 50% <= 2/3 -> R4 fails -> no honest node ever proposes r+2. The tick re-walk re-fetches V_k every tick and the latch drops it every tick. No new vertex means no evidence carrier (drain_evidence_for_vertex runs only inside a successful try_create_vertex, dag.rs:648), so the slash never lands and Z is never removed; even if it were, 2/3 of the remaining 3 is not > 2/3. Same arithmetic for any n: three groups of (n-1)/3, any node resolves two of them = 2(n-1)/3 < 2n/3. Cost to Z: three signatures.
which_invariant: I9 (equivocation must never create a citable-but-unobtainable hash) and I2
design_section: §6 'Shadow storage': 'at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart'; §7 row 1; dag.rs:1143-1168, 2287-2290
design_fix: Bound shadows per (author, round) by the number of DISTINCT twins actually cited by held vertices (each additional twin costs the attacker one honest citer, so the bound is <= number of validators), not by a constant 1; store any twin that some held round-(r+1) body cites. Alternatively make R1 treat 'cites a twin of a known equivocator at (author, round)' as resolved once ANY twin is held (the cone then contains whichever twins are held, which is why fix #2 must be applied first). Test `three_way_equivocation_does_not_halt`: n=4, three twins split 1:1:1, assert every honest node proposes r+2 and identical anchors; mutation: cap shadows at 1.

title: Exclude-on-timeout until TTL, combined with the unreserved 100-slot TCP accept cap, lets two IPs stop every honest fetch and therefore every honest proposal
attack: Unauthenticated attacker opens 60 sessions from IP-a and 40 from IP-b to each validator (network/src/lib.rs:108-131: MAX_CONNECTIONS=100 checked before the per-IP cap of 60), sends the 32-byte ephemeral key so the handshake completes, then idles; the server's frame-length read times out after 60 s (lib.rs:211-215) so the attacker reconnects every 59 s (or holds the 10 s handshake window, lib.rs:159-166). Every honest `secure_connect` to that validator is accepted by the kernel and immediately dropped by the `continue` at lib.rs:108-113 -> EOF/timeout inside the 2-tick deadline. §5.4 then excludes that peer 'for that hash, until TTL' (64 ticks = 192 s at the 3 s tick); the next attempt hits the next witness, also starved; within 2-3 attempts every witness and every 'validator with peer_ip' is excluded and the WANTED entry idles to TTL, is evicted, is re-inserted by the tick re-walk, and repeats. Meanwhile Part I's R4 stops any node that cannot resolve > 2/3 of round-(r-1) from proposing, and ordinary 5 % loss (design §1) produces a hole on some validator every few rounds. Result: chain-wide proposal stop for as long as ~200 idle sockets are held, at ~zero bandwidth, with no validator key. Stage 3 ships before Stage 5 (§11), so this window is real; and even after slot reservation the exclusion rule converts every transient failure (Pi under load, NAT reset) into a 64-tick blacklist. If the fetcher classifies the EOF as an error rather than a timeout, backoff min(2^k,16) ticks gives the same outcome with a 16-tick recovery lag.
which_invariant: I15 (unauthenticated peers must not deny fetch service) and I2 (pull must reach a holder)
design_section: §5.4 'Exclude for that hash, until TTL, any peer that timed out…'; §9 I15 'TCP slots = Stage 5'; §11 ordering; network/src/lib.rs:108-131, 159-166, 211-215
design_fix: Never exclude a peer on timeout or connect failure — exclude only on an explicit `unknown` or an invalid body, and even then for a short bounded window (e.g. 4 ticks), with per-peer backoff instead of per-hash exclusion. Make Stage 5 (validator-reserved accept slots: reserve n slots for sessions whose HELLO authenticates as a current validator, evict the oldest unauthenticated session when full) a prerequisite of Stage 3, not a follow-up. Test `slot_exhaustion_does_not_blacklist_holders`: fill the target's accept cap from two IPs, assert Tier A fetch completes within the TTL once one slot frees; mutation: exclude on timeout.

title: All Part II timers are in receiver ticks, but the tick is an operator knob (100 ms floor) and one fetch needs 4 WAN round trips plus a 1 MiB body
attack: Tick = AINCORE_CONSENSUS_TICK_MS, default 3000, floor 100 (main.rs:633-637); the burn-in ran at 500 ms (dag.rs:766-777 records exactly this class of bug: 'a liveness knob must not silently change meaning when a performance knob is turned'). One fetch = TCP connect (1 RTT) + client ephemeral -> server hello (1 RTT) + HELLO -> WELCOME (1 RTT) + VERTEX_REQ -> VERTEX_RESP (1 RTT) (network/src/lib.rs:426-540, 207-233) = 4 RTT = 600 ms on the design's 150 ms WAN, plus two Ed25519 sign/verify, plus up to 1 MiB of reply on a Pi uplink (20 Mbit/s ≈ 420 ms). At 500 ms tick the 2-tick deadline is 1.0 s: a full-size honest response (one 768 KiB vertex) misses it; the holder is excluded until TTL (64 ticks = 32 s); the second witness is tried and excluded; the entry dies. At the 100 ms floor the deadline (200 ms) is below one RTT chain, so no WAN fetch ever completes, TTL is 6.4 s, and Tier B's 'one frame per 16 ticks' is 1.6 s. No attacker is needed; the stall is worst for the largest (fullest) vertices, i.e. under load. Conversely at a 3 s tick the deadline (6 s) exceeds the 5 s connect timeout but is far below the transport's 120 s frame timeouts, so the abort must actively cancel the task or the socket and pool slot leak for up to 120 s.
which_invariant: I3 / I14 (timing must be on a quantity the receiver controls and must not silently change meaning); I2
design_section: §5.4 'Per-request deadline: 2 receiver ticks'; §5.2 'TTL of 64 ticks', 'one frame per 16 ticks'; main.rs:633-637; dag.rs:766-777; network/src/lib.rs:15-18, 426-540
design_fix: Define fetch timers in wall time with a floor independent of the tick: deadline = max(2 ticks, 5 s) (or 4 × measured RTT to that peer + size/bandwidth estimate), TTL = max(64 ticks, 180 s), Tier B frame interval = max(16 ticks, 30 s); document that the tick is a proposal cadence, not a network RTT. Cancel the socket on deadline (tokio::time::timeout around the whole connect+request future) so pool slots are released. Test `fetch_deadline_at_100ms_tick_over_150ms_link` with a delayed-socket harness; mutation: deadline in ticks only.

title: VERTEX_REQ server has no per-peer byte or CPU budget: ~450x amplification saturates a Raspberry Pi validator from one unauthenticated connection
attack: Any TCP client that completes the X25519 exchange may send requests (research B: `__`-prefixed ids are accepted; no validator key needed). Per connection the transport allows 100 msg/s (network/src/lib.rs:207-233); the design allows 32 hashes per request and a reply up to 1 MiB (§5.3), served from storage with no consensus lock. Attacker sends VERTEX_REQ for 32 real 768 KiB hashes (learned from gossip) at 100 req/s: server does up to 64 RocksDB gets, JSON-serialises up to 32 × 768 KiB = 24 MiB per request unless it trims incrementally (the design does not say; nothing forbids the same hash 32 times), then ChaCha20-Poly1305-encrypts (crypto/transport.rs:1-2) and writes 1 MiB. Per connection: 100 MiB/s ≈ 840 Mbit/s egress and ≈ 100 MiB/s AEAD + serde. A Cortex-A72 core does ~150-250 MB/s ChaCha20-Poly1305 and comparable serde throughput, so one connection pins ≥ 1 core and the NIC; four connections from ONE IP (cap 60) pin all four cores. Request bytes ≈ 2.3 KB -> reply 1 MiB: ≈ 450× amplification, paid by the victim's uplink, so its own DAG_VERTEX broadcasts, QC votes, and honest VERTEX_RESPs to peers are starved. The ticker (`consensus.write()` every tick) and the gossip consumer share those cores. §7 dismisses 'VERTEX_REQ flood' with '§5 quotas', but every §5 quota is requester-side; §9 marks I15 'server cost bounded'. (SYNC_REQ at sync/src/lib.rs:1213-1218 has the same shape today — 500 blocks, no byte cap — so this is not a new class, but Part II adds a second, hash-addressable instance and claims the bound.)
which_invariant: I15 (unauthenticated peers must not deny service) / I4 (byte-bounded)
design_section: §5.3 Messages; §7 'VERTEX_REQ flood'; §9 I15; network/src/lib.rs:207-233, 239; sync/src/lib.rs:1213-1218
design_fix: Server-side: reject requests with duplicate hashes; cap hashes per request at 8 and serve at most one MAX_VERTEX_BYTES body per reply beyond the first (trim while serialising, never build then trim); a per-connection byte budget (e.g. 4 MiB per 10 s) and a per-IP request budget (e.g. 20 req/s) enforced in the handler; prefer serving from a small LRU of pre-serialised `vertex:{H}` strings so a hot hash costs no serde; unauthenticated sessions get a lower budget than sessions whose HELLO authenticates as a validator. State the Pi numbers in §12. Test `vertex_req_flood_keeps_tick_under_100ms`: 4 attacker connections at 100 req/s, assert ticker latency and honest fetch completion; mutation: remove the byte budget.

title: I10 rejoin claim is false: peers prune below finalized−10, so any gap > ~10 rounds is unfetchable, and the 'round < prune_horizon' exit is computed on a field the fetcher cannot observe
attack: Progressing validators call prune_dag(min(finalized, latest_block_round) − 10) every 10 blocks (dag.rs:1786-1808, 2770-2783), deleting both `dag` entries and `vertex:{H}` rows. A validator that restarts after G > 10 rounds (30 s at the 3 s tick; the catalogued I10 case is 30-60 rounds) comes back with committed_set at its old cursor. Test row `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` disables ChainSync, so committed_set never moves. Every round-(current−1) candidate's resolve_walk (floor 0, §3) descends through the band [old cursor, current) ; every hash below every peer's horizon is answered `unknown` by all holders, excluded until TTL, and never fills. R4 is therefore never met, the node never proposes, and its own try_commit cannot advance because the lowest anchor's cone is in the pruned band — exactly the wedge I10 describes, now made permanent by Part I's R4 instead of by parent_quorum. Even inside the retention window the design descends one level per tick (§5.5: 'invalidate … re-walk those on the next tick'; §5.1: the trigger is the once-per-tick proposer walk), so a 10-round band costs ≥ 10 ticks during which 10 new rounds arrive; with ChainSync on this converges only because sync adoption moves the floor, i.e. I10 is carried by HEAD's ChainSync path, not by Part II. Finally §5.4's exit 'round < prune_horizon' refers to the absent body's round, which §5.2 itself says is unobservable ('defined on what the node can observe … not on the absent body's fields'); as written the exit never fires and the entry lives to TTL.
which_invariant: I10 (re-entry from a gap larger than any re-gossip window) and I2
design_section: §5.4 exit conditions; §5.5 release timing; §9 row I10 'boot walk + fetch'; §10 row `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync`; dag.rs:1786-1808, 2770-2783; ordering.rs:697-702
design_fix: State the fetch window explicitly: vertex fetch heals holes with citer.round − 1 ≥ (network finalized − 10); anything deeper is healed only by ChainSync adoption (settled-without-body), which must therefore remain mandatory and the test row must be rewritten as 'gap ≤ retention window' or dropped. Compute the exit as `citer.round − 1 < prune_horizon` (observable). Add a VERTEX_RESP `below_horizon` per-hash signal (mirroring SyncResponse.prune_horizon) so the requester stops asking and triggers block sync immediately. Re-walk on admission inside the fetcher (bounded to the released dependents) rather than on the next tick, so a k-level band resolves in k fetch RTTs, not k ticks. Test: restart with G = 40 rounds, ChainSync ON, assert the node proposes within 20 ticks; mutation: exit on unobservable round.

title: Serving `vertex_shadow:{H}` returns a compact-form body that the requester's single gate rejects, so honest shadow-holders get blacklisted as invalid-body senders
attack: §5.3 has the server answer from `vertex:{H}` OR `vertex_shadow:{H}`, and §6 stores the shadow as 'compact form plus parents' (payload_root/parents_root set, payload stripped, blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461). §5.3 also mandates that every fetched body 'enters through handle_message — the single gate'. add_vertex rejects any body with `!vertex.is_live_form()` at dag.rs:1036-1042 ('live vertex carries proof-only root fields') before the equivocation branch; the compact body also fails the recomputed-hash check at dag.rs:1062-1070 because parents/payload are empty. Sequence: N4 lacks twin V'; witnesses are excluded (timeout or slot exhaustion, finding 4); fallback 'validators with peer_ip' includes N1, which holds V' only as a shadow; N1 serves the compact row; N4's gate rejects it; §5.4 then excludes N1 'until TTL' for 'returned an invalid body'. The one serving path the design added for shadows is thus dead and actively poisons peer selection; the requester can only ever obtain a twin from a node that holds it live in `dag`. Under the two-way split that node exists, but combined with finding 4 the honest live holders are already excluded, so the entry starves.
which_invariant: I6 (single gate) / I2 (pull from a holder)
design_section: §5.3 'vertex:{H} or vertex_shadow:{H}'; §6 'Shadow storage'; dag.rs:1036-1042, 1062-1070; blockchain/src/lib.rs:439-441, 454-461
design_fix: Store shadows as full live bodies (also required by finding 2) so `vertex_shadow:{H}` serves something the gate accepts; or drop `vertex_shadow:` from the serving set and have the requester ask only witnesses that cite the twin (they hold it live). Never blacklist a peer for a body that fails the live-form check when the requester itself knows (author, round) is a twin pair; count it as `unknown`. Test: fetch a twin from a shadow-only holder and assert admission and no exclusion; mutation: serve compact form.

title: Three-way leader equivocation: one-shadow bound makes the twin set arrival-ordered again (fork) and the third twin permanently unadmittable (WANTED never releases, R4 fails everywhere)
attack: n=4, stakes N1=10%, N2=10%, N3=55%, O=25%; O leads even round r. O signs THREE round-r bodies A,B,C and delivers A→N1, B→N2, C→N3 first over direct TCP, then lets gossipsub carry the rest. Per §6 each node keeps its first body in `dag`, the FIRST counterpart as its single shadow, and drops every further same-(author,round) body via the `sys:equiv_seen` latch (dag.rs:2287-2290, `apply_equivocation_slash` returns before any write). Result: N1={A dag, B shadow}, N2={B dag, C shadow}, N3={C dag, A shadow}. At r+1 each honest node cites its own dag twin; O withholds its r+1 vertex. E1 at N1 returns T={A,B}; at N2 T={B,C}; at N3 T={C,A} — the twin set is a function of arrival order, the exact v2 root cause. E2 at N1: held r+1 stake = 75% ≥ 2/3, Σ_T votes = votes(A)+votes(B) = 20% ≤ 1/3 → SKIP r (the vote for C held in N3's r+1 body is not counted because C∉T). E2 at N2/N3: Σ_T = 65% > 1/3, none > 2/3 → defer. N1 advances the cursor past r and commits later anchors; N2/N3 never do → divergent committed sequences and `anchor_hash` per height, i.e. fork, with one Byzantine validator and no packet loss. Independently of the fork: N1 walks N3's r+1 vertex → blocked on C → WANTED[C] Tier A (witness N3 = 55% > 1/3) → fetched from N3 → enters `handle_message` → equivocation branch → dropped by the latch → no admission, no settlement → §5.5 release never fires; WANTED[C] TTLs out and is re-created every tick (bounded infinite fetch loop). Every honest node can resolve only the r+1 vertices whose twin it holds (dag or its one shadow): with a k≥3-way split each node's resolvable round-(r+1) stake ≤ 2/k ≤ 2/3 → R4 fails on every honest node forever → nobody proposes at r+2 → chain halt even in the equal-stake case where E2 does not fork.
which_invariant: I9 (equivocation must never create a citable-but-unobtainable hash — C is cited by N3 and unobtainable by N1/N2), I1 (an admitted citer whose parent can never be held), I5/I6 (a fetched body that reaches the gate but is never 'admitted' so no release signal exists). Design claim broken: §7 row 2 'Arrival order irrelevant'.
design_section: §6 'Shadow storage' (at most one shadow per (author, round); further bodies dropped without writing via dag.rs:2287-2290), §6 E1 (T over `dag ∪ shadow`), §6 E2 skip rule (Σ over T only), §5.5 release (admission-or-settlement only), §7 row 2, §10 `leader_equivocation_A3_B1/_A2_B2`.
design_fix: (1) Shadow slots must be demand-driven, not first-come: any hash in WANTED whose fetched body is an equivocating twin is stored as a shadow (compact+parents) — bound per (author, round) by the number of DISTINCT round-r hashes cited by held round-(r+1) bodies (≤ n, and the offender is slashed, so per-offender ≤ n×(rounds in window)); never drop a body that some held vertex cites. (2) E2 must not skip on a twin set that is incomplete relative to the held votes: define T as the set of round-r parents cited by held round-(r+1) bodies whose author is leader(r) — which requires those parent bodies to be held — and require that EVERY round-r parent cited by the walked ≥2/3 round-(r+1) set is held (i.e. the r+1 set is fully resolved at round r) before the ≤1/3 skip proof is accepted; otherwise defer and WANTED the unheld cited parents (these ARE observable by hash, unlike 'missing votes'). (3) Add test `leader_equivocation_three_way_split` asserting identical anchor_hash for r on all nodes with the mutation 'keep only the first counterpart shadow'.

title: E2 is not total: a leader-equivocation split with no twin > 2/3 and Σ > 1/3 while every round-(r+1) body is held is a permanent defer — chain halt with one Byzantine leader who withholds its own r+1 vote
attack: n=4 equal stake, O leads even round r, twins A (→N1,N2) and B (→N3) via gossipsub race; O emits NO round-(r+1) vertex. Per Part II each honest node holds both twins (dag + shadow) after fetch, so T={A,B} identically everywhere — E1 fine. E2: held round-(r+1) stake = 75% ≥ 2/3; votes(A)=50%, votes(B)=25%; Σ=75% > 1/3 and neither > 2/3 → 'Otherwise defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes'. There are NO missing votes: every round-(r+1) body that will ever exist is held (O's is withheld and O can never be forced to produce it). Defer is permanent. try_commit step 1 (ordering.rs:558-567) scans past r to a later direct anchor, but step 2 (:583-597) must decide r on the walk back and per §6 'never decides a twinned round by visited membership' → E2 → defer → `return out`. No anchor ≥ r ever commits; the block-carried slash for O (dag.rs:2046, executor:2266-2339) needs a block, which needs a commit → the slash never lands either. Works for any n: any split with max_t votes(t) ≤ 2/3 and Σ > 1/3, which the offender can steer by its own vote (and which gossipsub races produce naturally at n=4 without steering, e.g. 2:2 with O voting). Also: the 'WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes' branch has no mechanism even when votes ARE missing — WANTED is keyed by hash and try_commit holds no hash for a vertex it never saw; the only hash source is a citer at r+2, which is Part I's proposer walk, not try_commit.
which_invariant: I1 (the commit path encounters a state from which it can never advance, created by admitted vertices), I9 (equivocation wedges commit on all sides). Design claim broken: §7 row 2 'commits r at the twin with > 2/3 votes, or skips if ≤ 1/3 total, or defers and fetches votes' — the middle band (1/3, 2/3] with a complete vote set has no exit; §10 `leader_equivocation_A2_B2` asserts 'commit or skip' for a case E2 cannot decide.
design_section: §6 Rule E2 (three bullets), §7 row 2, §10 rows `leader_equivocation_A3_B1` / `_A2_B2`.
design_fix: E2 needs a total, cone-determined rule for the middle band. Bullshark's answer is the one v3 threw away, made twin-safe: when a LATER direct anchor r' commits, decide twinned round r by the anchor chain's complete causal history (walk_history floor r, which Part I now guarantees completes): if exactly one twin is in the cone → commit at it; if none → skip; if more than one twin is in the cone (possible only when the cone's own citers split) → deterministic tiebreak by lowest hash. This is arrival-order-independent because it is a pure function of the complete cone, the same argument §7 row 1 already makes for non-leader offenders; quorum intersection still guarantees consistency with any node that committed directly at t (t is in every later cone). Keep the direct-vote fast path only as an optimisation. Drop the 'WANTED the missing votes' text or replace it with 'WANTED the unheld round-r parents cited by held r+1 bodies'. Add mutation test: 2:1 honest split with the offender's r+1 vertex withheld; assert commit-or-skip identical on all nodes within 2 anchors; mutation = 'defer when Σ∈(1/3,2/3]'.

title: Boot loops set current_round from the maximum replayed vertex round; one admitted far-future vertex plus a routine restart silences the Part II trigger — the restarted validator never walks, never WANTs, never proposes until the network reaches that round
attack: Attacker validator sends ONE vertex V with round = current_round + 9_999 (passes the jump guard dag.rs:963 `≤ current + MAX_ROUND_JUMP`, PWN-003 future-timestamp check, signature, non-empty parents, membership). It is persisted at `vertex:{H}` (dag.rs:1170) and gossiped to every node. Ingress fast-forward is quorum-gated (:1231-1240) so nothing happens live. Then any node restarts (rolling deploy, the memory notes one reboot froze the chain for 10 days). All three boot loops do `if vertex.round > max_round { max_round = vertex.round }` unconditionally (dag.rs:224, :271, :337) and `final_start_round = max(1, max_round + 1)` (:430-437) → current_round = current+10_000. `try_create_vertex` (:529-536) takes `round_index[current−1]` = [V] only; parent_quorum_met false → below-quorum branch (:881) forever. Part II's only trigger is 'the proposer's own resolve_walk' over round-(current−1) candidates (§5.1, §3 (c)): the sole candidate is V, whose walk blocks on V's fake parents → WANTED with witness = attacker → Tier B → attacker answers `unknown` → TTL. Nothing else is ever WANTed because there are no other candidates at that round. `add_vertex` fast-forward (:1231) and `reload_chain_tip` (:3001 `if next_round > self.current_round`) only ever RAISE current_round; live vertices at the real round are admitted but are 10_000 rounds below the proposal clock. The node commits (cursor-driven) but never proposes; at 3 s ticks that is ≥ 8 hours of exclusion per restart. Every node received V, so a rolling restart of validators holding > 1/3 stake halts the chain (R4 on the remaining nodes cannot reach > 2/3 cited stake). The comment at dag.rs:2937-2946 already records that closing one door (ingress) then a second (reload) was 'not enough'; the boot loop is the third door and it is wide open.
which_invariant: I10 (a restarted validator must be able to re-enter without already holding recent vertices) — the design's I10 row claims 'boot walk (bounded ≤ current+2) + fetch'; I11 is cited by the design as the far-future bound but I11 is a BYTES bound and does not cover the boot round derivation; I14 (recovery must not depend on the failing event: the proposal clock can only be corrected by proposing).
design_section: §5.1 trigger (proposer walk only), §5.2 '(far-future admitted vertices are the I11 bound, tracked separately)', §9 I10 row 'boot walk (bounded ≤ current+2) + fetch', §10 row `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync`, §12 I11 bullet.
design_fix: Derive the boot round the same way ingress and reload do: after replay, `current_round = max(quorum_round(round_idx, dag, validators) + 1, latest_proposed_round + 1)` — never `max_round + 1` — with `latest_proposed_round` itself only ever written from quorum-gated paths (it already is: :1237, :3006). Additionally clamp replayed far-future vertices at boot: do not index a vertex with `round > quorum_round + MAX_ROUND_JUMP/2` into `round_index` (keep it in storage, or drop it — it can never become a parent). Add a Part II trigger that does not depend on the proposal clock: also walk round-(quorum_round) candidates, so a wrong `current_round` cannot starve WANTED. Test: one far-future vertex, restart, assert the node proposes within 4 ticks and WANTED is populated from the live round; mutation = 'boot from max_round'.

title: Tier B 'from the author only' is unreachable for an author without a routable `peer_ip`; a self-vertex lost everywhere then makes every later vertex of that author unresolvable on every node, permanently — zombie validator, and a second one halts the chain
attack: n=4; validator X is behind NAT and dials OUT to N1..N3 (the documented multi-machine topology). N1..N3 hold only inbound sessions from X, so `storage.get_peer_ip(X)` is None on all of them — exactly the case sync/src/lib.rs:626-632 skips because 'their accepted socket source is not a routable sync target'. X's round-r vertex X_r is broadcast once (dag.rs:1884) and lost at all three (gossipsub mesh flap; the memory notes this exact one-shot loss bootstrapped a live deadlock). X is above quorum so it never re-gossips (:881 branch only fires below quorum). X_{r+1} cites X_r (X holds it). On N1: resolve_walk(X_{r+1}) → blocked on X_r; witnesses = {X} = 25% ≤ 1/3 → Tier B → request X only → `secure_connect(peer_ip(X)…)` has no address → cannot request; Tier A never applies because nobody but X will ever cite X_{r+1} (Part I: honest nodes cite only resolved vertices). Every subsequent X_{r+k} chains through X_{r+1} → X_r, so with the floor-0 walk EVERY future X vertex is Unresolved on N1..N3 forever. Consequences: X's stake is never cited (R4 on honest nodes runs on 75% — one more loss of any kind and R4 fails everywhere → halt); every even round X leads is skipped (§3.4: cited by no honest vertex → not in visited); X_r never enters any anchor cone so it never settles via commit or sync (committed_vertices come from cones), so the condition is permanent; X itself sees nothing wrong (its own walk resolves its chain) and keeps proposing into the void. Two NAT'd validators in this state at n=4 → cited stake ≤ 50% → chain halt with zero Byzantine actors.
which_invariant: I2 (redelivery must be a pull from a node that HOLDS the vertex — the only holder is unreachable and the design provides no holder-side push), I10 (re-entry must not depend on the node's own view — here X cannot even detect exclusion). Design claim broken: §10 row `self_vertex_lost_everywhere_fetched_from_author` and §12 'Partition: … deferral, never wedge'.
design_section: §5.2 Tier B (request it from X only), §5.4 'Whom: witnesses first…, then validators with `peer_ip`; Tier B: the author only', §5.3 (`secure_connect(…, Some(peer_id), …)`).
design_fix: Add the missing holder-side push, which I2 permits: a proposer that observes its own round-r vertex is cited by NO held round-(r+1) body from > 1/3 stake (observable from held bodies, O(n)) re-broadcasts that vertex once per 16 ticks (bounded, own-tick scheduled, idempotent at ingress by hash dedup at dag.rs:1143). Make Tier B fall back to 'any peer with a live session' (the inbound session itself is a valid reply channel — the request can be answered over the existing encrypted socket the author opened) rather than requiring `peer_ip`; and have the author advertise a routable address in its vertex or handshake so `peer_ip` exists for inbound-only peers. Test: X with no `peer_ip` on any peer, X_r dropped at all receivers, assert X_r admitted everywhere within 32 ticks and X's leader rounds not skipped; mutation = 'remove holder re-broadcast'.

title: Fetch can never bridge a gap deeper than the serving peer's prune margin (~10 rounds below its finality): the `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` row is unpassable and a minority partition > 10 rounds wedges without ChainSync
attack: Serving reads `vertex:{H}` (§5.3), and `prune_dag` deletes that row and the in-memory entry on every node for `round < min(finalized_round, latest_block_round) − 10` every 10 blocks (dag.rs:1786-1808, :2770-2783, `storage.delete` at :2779). Sequence per §10 row 15: 4 validators, N4 down 30 rounds with ChainSync 'fully disabled'. N4 restarts with `committed_set` at ≈ round R (its own last commits). Live vertices at R+30 arrive; after a quorum is held `current_round` = R+31 (dag.rs:1231-1240). Proposer walk from R+30 candidates descends the held band and blocks on all of R+29 → Tier A WANTED → fetched (peers hold ≥ F−10 ≈ R+18) → admitted → re-walk → R+28 … → R+18 fetched; R+17 and below: every peer answers `unknown` (rows deleted) → each peer excluded for that hash until TTL (§5.4) → entry expires at 64 ticks → recreated by the next tick's walk → infinite unknown loop. Because the walk is floor-0 and terminates only at `committed_set ∪ genesis` (§3), and committed_set cannot advance without either a local commit (impossible: try_commit's own walk_history has the same hole, ordering.rs:697-702) or sync adoption (disabled), N4 never resolves any round-(current−1) candidate → R4 fails forever → N4 never proposes again. The same happens with ChainSync ON whenever it cannot deliver: `gather_and_check_seed_tips` disagreement returns before any block (sync :607-622), all peers session-only (:626-632), or the peer has pruned below the node's height (:736-747, 'bootstrap from a state snapshot'). A 3:1 partition healed after > 10 rounds puts the minority node in exactly this state.
which_invariant: I10 (re-enter from a gap LARGER than any re-gossip window — here the serve window is only 10 rounds past the server's finality), I2 (pull from a holder — no holder exists once pruned, and the design has no path from a pruned hash to settlement). Design claim broken: §10 row 15 `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` ('gap > uncommitted cone; node rejoins via tick re-walk + fetch'), §12 'Partition: bounded probing; deferral, never wedge'.
design_section: §5.3 server (`vertex:{H}` or `vertex_shadow:{H}`), §5.4 exclusion/TTL and 'Exit on … `round < prune_horizon`' (unevaluable: the entry holds only a hash and the design itself says the absent body's fields are unobservable), §10 row 15, §12 partition bullet, §9 I10 row.
design_fix: State the dependency honestly: Part II fetch recovers only the uncommitted cone; anything below a serving peer's `min_round` must be SETTLED, not obtained. Add a `VERTEX_RESP.settled: [(hash, height)]` answer for pruned hashes (the server can map hash → block via `consensus:cseq:{round}` / block.committed_vertices while those rows exist, or a small hash→height index kept for the prune window), and on receipt the requester runs the existing QC-verified block adoption for that height (ChainSync's `apply_finality_artifact` + `adopt_synced_anchor`) — i.e. fetch-below-horizon forces the settlement path immediately instead of looping on `unknown`. Make `unknown` from > 1/3 stake for a hash trigger an immediate `sync_from_peers` rather than a 64-tick TTL. Rewrite row 15 to 'ChainSync serving only (no gossip), gap > cone' and add a row 'minority partition 3:1 healed after 40 rounds, all four converge'.

title: Sync-settlement release is keyed through WANTED[H].blocked; a hash that settles after its WANTED entry expired (or was never created) invalidates nothing, and the design leaves open whether a stale `Unresolved` cache entry short-circuits descendant walks
attack: Restart case from the previous hole with ChainSync ON but slow on the first pass (initial `sync_from_peers` waits 3 s, tip agreement, batch of 500 blocks executed synchronously in `process_blocks`). Tick t: proposer walk WANTs the pruned band hashes H_1..H_k; all peers answer `unknown`; entries carry `blocked = {C_1..C_n}` (the round-(current−1) candidates). Tick t+64: TTL evicts WANTED[H_i] (§5.2 'receiver-tick TTL of 64 ticks regardless of tier'). Tick t+70: `reload_chain_tip` adopts the synced blocks; `committed_set` now contains H_1..H_k. §5.5 release runs 'On … sync settlement of H: remove WANTED[H], invalidate resolved entries listed in blocked' — WANTED[H] no longer exists, so no `blocked` list, so no invalidation; the cache still holds `Unresolved{blocked_on ⊇ H_i}` for C_1..C_n and for every intermediate vertex the walk cached on the way down. If `resolve_walk` short-circuits on a cached `Unresolved` sub-entry (the only way the stated bound 'n walks per tick' is cheaper than n × full-cone re-descents at n=100), then every later candidate whose cone passes through those vertices inherits the stale verdict, (c) re-walks the top-level candidate but hits the same stale sub-entries, and the node never resolves > 2/3 again. The same gap exists for hashes that never entered WANTED because of the Tier A budget (256), the per-author quota, or the `> current_round + 2` exclusion.
which_invariant: I8 (a hash settling via SYNC must release dependents exactly as arrival does — release here is conditional on an unrelated, sender-influenceable lifetime), I7 (release must be keyed by the settled hash: the key must be the cache's reverse index, not WANTED).
design_section: §5.5 Release, §3 cache invalidation rule (b), §5.2 TTL/quota/`> current+2` exclusions, §8 'Sync sweep: lookup + invalidate'.
design_fix: Keep the reverse index `blocked_on → {dependent vertex hashes}` inside the `resolved` cache itself (Part I already needs it for rule (b), which has no WANTED), and have the sync hook iterate `block.committed_vertices` against THAT index; WANTED removal is a side effect, not the key. Specify explicitly that `resolve_walk` never short-circuits on a cached `Unresolved` sub-entry unless that entry's `blocked_on` hashes are all still absent from `dag ∪ shadow ∪ committed_set` (a cheap O(|blocked_on|) recheck), so a stale verdict can never survive a settlement it missed. Add a mutation row: 'TTL-expire WANTED before adoption; assert candidates re-resolve after adoption with 0 add_vertex calls' (extends `sync_settlement_rewalks_blocked`).

title: E2 skip rule is unsound: a node can skip round r while another already committed it directly (v3's own 'arrival order irrelevant' claim is false)
which_invariant: I9 (and §12 'never wedge or fork'); the §7 row-2 claim 'Arrival order irrelevant' and §6 'quorum intersection proves no direct quorum for any twin ever existed'
design_section: §6 Rule E2 (skip branch); §7 row 2; §10 rows `leader_equivocation_A3_B1` / `_A2_B2`
attack: n=4 equal stake (H1,H2,H3 honest, V Byzantine, V = leader(r)). stake_quorum_met (qc.rs:194-196) makes '>2/3' = 3 of 4, '≥2/3 held' = 3 of 4, '≤1/3' = 1 of 4. V signs twins A (parents = the three honest round-(r-1) vertices) and B (parents include one fake hash P). Both are admitted everywhere (admission is bytes-only, §3); B is a twin per E1 but resolves nowhere, so no honest node ever cites B. Deliveries: A → H1, H2 first. B → H3 first (H3 dag=B, later A as shadow once H1_{r+1} cites A and the walk fetches it). H3 cannot cite B (unresolved) and holds no A at proposal time, so H3_{r+1} cites {H1_r,H2_r,H3_r} = 3/4 > 2/3 (R4 satisfied) — cites NEITHER twin. V equivocates at r+1 too: V1 cites A → sent to H1,H2; V2 cites only the three honest round-r vertices → sent by direct TCP to H3. H1_{r+1}, H2_{r+1} cite A. Node H1's try_commit: held r+1 bodies {H1,H2,V1} all cite A → votes(A)=3 → E2 step 1 COMMITS r at A (ordering.rs:558-567 per twin). Node H3's try_commit on the tick where V2 has arrived but H2_{r+1} has not yet (5% gossip loss is routine, and V's direct TCP beats gossipsub): held r+1 = {H1_{r+1}(A), H3_{r+1}(none), V2(none)} = 3/4 ≥ 2/3; Σ votes = 1 ≤ 1/3 → E2 SKIPS r; cursor advances past r permanently (apply_anchor_bookkeeping next_anchor_round). H1 has anchor_hash=A at r, H3 has no anchor at r → finality digests diverge → block-level fork. The arithmetic: >2/3 voters ∩ ≥2/3 held is only >1/3 stake, of which up to f is Byzantine (V's r+1 twin is different on each node), leaving honest overlap >1/3−f, which is < the 1/3 the skip tolerates. This is exactly v2's root cause (a decision that depends on which r+1 body of an equivocator each node holds) restated as a vote count. Neither `leader_equivocation_A3_B1` nor `_A2_B2` can fail on this: they do not give V an r+1 twin, do not include an honest r+1 vertex citing no twin, and do not stage H2_{r+1}'s arrival after V2's — the split they test never reaches the skip branch with a concurrent direct commit.
design_fix: Skip a twinned round r only when, for EVERY twin t, the distinct-author stake of held round-(r+1) bodies that do NOT cite t is > 2/3 (then any >2/3 voter set for t would intersect it in >1/3 > f, containing an honest author whose r+1 vertex is identical everywhere — contradiction). '≥2/3 held and Σ ≤ 1/3' is not that condition. Add the test above (V equivocates at r AND r+1; one honest r+1 citer of neither twin; V2 delivered before H2_{r+1}) and assert identical anchor_hash-or-skip across nodes.

title: E2 has no terminal decision when all r+1 votes are held and split: one equivocation permanently halts the chain (and test A2_B2 asserts an outcome E2 never produces)
which_invariant: I1 (no anchor commits again) via Part II's own §12 'deferral, never wedge'; I9
design_section: §6 Rule E2 ('Otherwise defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes'); §10 row `leader_equivocation_A2_B2`
attack: n=4, V = leader(r), both twins fully valid. V sends A to H1,H2 and B to H3; V's own r+1 vertex cites B. After §5 fetch every node holds both twins. Held r+1 bodies: H1_{r+1}(A), H2_{r+1}(A), H3_{r+1}(B), V_{r+1}(B) — votes(A)=2, votes(B)=2, neither ≥3; held = 4 ≥ 2/3; Σ=4 > 1/3 → not skip → 'defer and WANTED the missing votes' — there are no missing votes. try_commit decides strictly in round order from the persisted cursor, ONE anchor per call (ordering.rs:527-620): r is in [cursor, r_direct) for every later direct anchor and step 2 'never decides a twinned round by visited', so every call returns empty at r forever. No anchor ≥ r ever commits on any node; cost to V is one 100% slash for a permanent global halt. Even with V not voting (2:1:absent) Σ=3 > 1/3 still defers forever. Row `leader_equivocation_A2_B2` asserts 'commit at the >2/3 twin, or skip' for a 2:2 split — under E2 the only 2:2 that commits is when V's vote makes 3 for one twin; the V-votes-minority 2:2 never terminates, so the test as specified either hangs or is written to accept a permanent defer, and either way cannot fail on this wedge.
design_fix: A twinned round needs an ancestry-based fallback that is a pure function of a later committed anchor's cone, as in Mysticeti's certified-support / indirect rule (A-reference-designs: 'at most one twin can gather 2f+1 support'): when no twin has >2/3 direct votes and the sound skip condition (hole 1) does not hold, decide r from the next committed anchor's cone by the certificate pattern inside the cone, never by raw held votes. Add a test where votes split with no twin reaching quorum and assert the chain continues past r identically on all nodes.

title: Compact shadow twin has no payload and is invisible to find_causal_history and the block builder: any committed cone containing the second twin forks the sequence or the executed transactions
which_invariant: I9 (twin cited by peers must be obtainable and orderable identically); §6 'the sequence orders whatever the cone contains'
design_section: §6 Shadow storage ('compact form plus parents — the walk needs parents, not payload'); §6 last paragraph; §8
attack: n=4, V equivocates at any round r (need not be leader): A → H1,H2 first; B → H3 first. B's parents are honest round-(r−1) vertices, so B resolves at H3 and H3_{r+1} cites B (R4). Anchor r+2 (an honest leader) cites ≥3 r+1 vertices including H3_{r+1}; every node commits anchor r+2 and its cone contains B. At H3, B ∈ dag. At H1/H2, B was fetched (§5) and stored as a SHADOW in compact form: `to_compact_proof` (blockchain/src/lib.rs:454-461) sets payload=[] and payload_root=Some. Now: (a) `find_causal_history` (ordering.rs:964-990) and `walk_history` (:683-718) read `dag.get` only — the design only says `resolve_walk` and E1/E2 read dag ∪ shadow — so on H1 the sequence for anchor r+2 omits B while H3's includes it → `fold_finality_digest` differs → finality fork; or, if the author extends those walks to dag ∪ shadow, (b) the block builder (dag.rs:1345-1385) does `dag.get(hash)` per sequence hash and pushes `v.payload` into block_txs; B is not in `dag` on H1 → COMMIT_VERTEX_MISSING (:1375-1384) and zero transactions, or if it also reads shadow, an empty compact payload — while H3 executes B's full payload → different block_txs, state root and block hash at the same height. No deterministic 'drop twin payloads' rule can rescue this either: twin-knowledge at commit time is itself arrival-dependent (a node whose cone contains only B-citers never learns A is a twin). Additionally, a compact body served from `vertex_shadow:{H}` (§5.3) to a third node enters through `handle_message` → add_vertex and is rejected by the live-form check (dag.rs:1033-1042), so the shadow cannot even propagate.
design_fix: Shadow rows must hold the FULL body (bounded: one per (author, round) within the unpruned window × MAX_VERTEX_BYTES, paid for by a 100% slash), and every reader of the committed cone — walk_history, find_causal_history, the block builder's payload assembly, and the VERTEX_RESP server — must read dag ∪ shadow uniformly. Add a test: second twin committed via a peer's citation; assert identical sequence, block_txs and state root on the node holding it as shadow vs. the node holding it in dag.

title: One-shadow-per-(author,round) plus 'further bodies dropped without writing' recreates I9: a third twin (or a phantom EQUIV_PROOF consuming the slot) makes an honestly-cited hash unobtainable forever
which_invariant: I9 (equivocation must never create a citable-but-unobtainable hash); I5
design_section: §6 Shadow storage ('at most one shadow per (author, round) — the first counterpart; any further same-round body from that author is dropped without writing (dag.rs:2287-2290)'); §10 row `phantom_proof_does_not_change_anchors`
attack: n=4. V signs three valid bodies A, B, C at round r, each citing honest round-(r−1) vertices, and delivers A→H1, B→H2, C→H3 by direct TCP first, then gossips all three. H1: dag=A, shadow=B (first counterpart), C dropped without writing and latched durably (sys:equiv_seen, dag.rs:2287-2290 — persisted, survives restart). H2: dag=B, shadow=A or C, the third dropped. H3: dag=C, shadow=?, third dropped. Each honest node cites its dag twin under R4: H1_{r+1}→A, H2_{r+1}→B, H3_{r+1}→C. Any later anchor cites ≥3 r+1 vertices → its cone contains all three twins. Every honest node is missing one: resolve_walk → WANTED → VERTEX_RESP → handle_message → add_vertex: dedup over dag ∪ shadow misses, equivocation branch fires, shadow already present → dropped again. walk_history in commit_one_anchor never completes → every node defers forever → global halt for one slash. Cheaper variant if shadows are written on `handle_remote_equivocation` (§6 says 'on equivocation detection', which includes dag.rs:2404-2457): only two twins needed — attacker sends EQUIV_PROOF(A, P) with a signed never-gossiped P to H1 alone, consuming H1's one shadow slot, then delivers real B to H2 first; H2 cites B; H1 drops B forever. Row `phantom_proof_does_not_change_anchors` cannot fail on this: it sends the phantom proof but never follows it with a real, honestly-cited second twin.
design_fix: Bound shadows per (author, round) by n (the number of distinct twins honest r+1 vertices can cite is ≤ n−1), or admit any twin that a HELD vertex cites (walk-driven admission), never a fixed 1. Never let a compact EQUIV_PROOF body occupy a shadow slot. Test: three twins delivered to three different nodes first, then an anchor whose cone spans all three; assert commit on all nodes.

title: I10 is not satisfied: fetch cannot recover vertices peers have pruned, so a validator down longer than the prune window never rejoins without ChainSync; `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` cannot pass
which_invariant: I10 (re-enter from a gap larger than any re-gossip window without already holding recent vertices)
design_section: §9 I10 row ('boot walk (bounded ≤ current+2) + fetch'); §10 row `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync`; §5.4 exit condition 'round < prune_horizon'
attack: Validator R goes down at round c (its committed_set ends at c) and returns after 60 rounds — the catalog's own I10 example. Peers prune every 10 blocks to `finalized − 10` (dag.rs:1786-1808) and `prune_dag` deletes `vertex:{H}` from disk and memory (dag.rs:2770-2783), so every vertex in (c, finalized−10) exists on no peer. R's resolve_walk (floor 0) for any tip candidate descends until it reaches R's committed_set — it must pass through those pruned rounds — and every hash there goes to WANTED; every VERTEX_RESP answers `unknown`; §5.4 excludes each peer for that hash until TTL, the entry dies at 64 ticks, and the §3 rule (c) tick re-walk re-inserts it next tick: an infinite request loop. R never resolves > 2/3 of any round, never proposes (R4), and its cursor never advances because walk_history in commit_one_anchor also hits the pruned hashes. The §5.4 exit 'round < prune_horizon' uses R's own stale horizon, so it never fires. The only mechanism that moves committed_set past a pruned region is adopt_synced_anchor from synced blocks (dag.rs:2852-2884) — precisely what row `restart_rejoin_without_chainsync` disables. Under that row's own conditions the test cannot pass; under 'gap > uncommitted cone' read narrowly (≤ ~10 rounds) it passes but does not test I10.
design_fix: State honestly that re-entry across a gap larger than the prune window is ChainSync adoption (committed_set advance) followed by fetch of the uncommitted cone only; make WANTED refuse hashes whose citing vertex round < (peer-reported or block-derived) finalized − 10 and route the node to sync instead; rewrite the row as `restart_rejoin_with_sync_adoption_then_fetch` with a 60-round gap.

title: validator_set_at(vertex.round) is not 'state identical on every node' for rounds above a lagging node's executed tip — Part I §3.2 hole that breaks Part II's I6 row and §5.3 admission
which_invariant: I6 ('admitted' must be identical on every node); the §3 premise 'admission is a pure function of the vertex bytes plus state identical on every node'
design_section: §5.3 ('membership evaluated by validator_set_at(vertex.round)'), §9 I6 row, §10 row `slashed_author_body_still_admissible_at_its_round`; root in Part I §3.2
attack: The snapshot `sys:validator_set_at:{round}` is written by the executor when the block whose anchor round is a executes (executor/src/lib.rs:2532-2580 rewrites the set at execution). Validator X is slashed by anchor a (height h). N1 has executed h; N2 lags one block (routine under catch-up). X's vertex X_r (r > a) arrives at both. validator_set_at(r) on N1 = the post-a snapshot (X absent) → ingress reject at dag.rs:1082 forever; on N2 the largest key ≤ r is the pre-a snapshot (X present) → admitted, and if X_r resolves N2 cites it under R4 and caches `Resolved` — 'authoritative until pruned' — so N2 keeps it even after executing h. N2_{r+1} now cites X_r; N1's walk hits X_r → WANTED → fetched from N2 → rejected again as invalid → N2 excluded until TTL. Any anchor whose cone includes N2_{r+1} wedges N1 (walk_history hole) while N2 and other lagging nodes commit it: admit-here/reject-there, the v2 #5 class the design claims closed. Also §3 says membership 'is not an ingress rejection' while §3.2/§5.3 say ingress uses validator_set_at — the design contradicts itself on which gate enforces it. Row `slashed_author_body_still_admissible_at_its_round` only tests round < slash round on a caught-up node and cannot fail here.
design_fix: Remove membership from ingress entirely (as §3 already claims); evaluate it only as a walk-edge check, and when the snapshot for parent.round is not yet available locally (round > last executed anchor round + 2) return Unresolved (defer), never a verdict, and never cache `Resolved` for a walk that used a provisional set. Test: slash at anchor a, N2 one block behind, X_r with r>a; assert both nodes reach the same admission and the same sequence after N2 catches up.

title: Tier B is single-shot: 'author only' plus 'exclude on timeout until TTL' gives one 2-tick attempt per 64 ticks, and an unauthenticated peer can force the timeout (I15 not done)
which_invariant: I2 (pull from a node that holds it — with no redundancy the pull is trivially denied); I15 dependency the design defers to Stage 5
design_section: §5.2 Tier B ('request it from X only'), §5.4 ('Exclude for that hash, until TTL, any peer that timed out'; deadline 2 ticks; TTL 64), §9 I15 row; §10 row `self_vertex_lost_everywhere_fetched_from_author`
attack: Honest X's vertex X_r is lost at every receiver (the row's own scenario). X_{r+1} cites it → Tier B WANTED[X_r] with X as the only permitted peer. Attacker (no key needed) fills X's 100 inbound TCP sessions (network/src/lib.rs:108, I15 open at HEAD, 'Stage 5' per §9), or X is simply slow: the single request misses the 2-tick deadline → X excluded for that hash until TTL → no other peer allowed → entry idles to 64 ticks, is deleted, and is re-created fresh by the next tick re-walk → next attempt. Effective rate: one attempt per ~64 ticks. Throughout, X_r and every X vertex above it are unresolvable everywhere, X's r+1.. vertices are never cited (R4), X's leader rounds are skipped by proof (no votes), and X earns no rewards — an unauthenticated peer excludes a validator from consensus for as long as it holds the slots. Row `self_vertex_lost_everywhere_fetched_from_author` runs in a lab without slot exhaustion and cannot fail on this.
design_fix: Tier B may target the author first but must fall back to any peer that has since admitted the body (peers that witnessed it become Tier A holders once they admit it), and the per-hash exclusion must not apply to the sole permitted peer; alternatively, make Stage 5 (I15 slot reservation) a prerequisite of Stage 3 rather than a follow-on. Test: X's inbound sessions saturated by a non-validator; assert X_r is still admitted within the TTL.

title: Fetch trigger is proposer-only and try_commit is inbound-driven: observers, jailed validators and partitioned nodes never populate WANTED, and E2's 'defer and WANTED' is never re-evaluated without traffic (I6/I14 recur)
which_invariant: I6 (release must work on validator AND observer nodes alike); I14 (timed actions must run independently of inbound traffic); I10 for a jailed validator
design_section: §5.1 ('The trigger is the proposer's own resolve_walk'; secondary trigger 'walk_history's hole in try_commit'); §9 I6, I10 rows
attack: At HEAD, `try_create_vertex` returns for a non-validator at dag.rs:607-612 (RULE 1) before the below-quorum branch, so the R4 evaluation and the §3 rule-(c) tick re-walk — Part II's primary WANTED source — never run on an observer (indexer, RPC, DEX, or a jailed validator, which is an observer until unjailed). The secondary trigger lives in try_commit, which is invoked only from add_vertex (dag.rs:1290) and is skipped outright on observers (:1242-1251). Sequence: indexer node loses one gossip vertex → its DAG has a permanent hole → no WANTED entry is ever created → local ordering (if enabled) defers forever; it serves state only via ChainSync adoption, which is the exact I6 failure ('orphans never drained on indexer/RPC/DEX/jailed nodes') with 'orphans' renamed 'holes'. Jailed validator: unjailed after N rounds, its DAG has N rounds of holes it never fetched → the hole-5 I10 loop begins from a worse position. Validators: E2's 'defer and WANTED the missing round-(r+1) votes' executes inside try_commit, which only runs when a vertex arrives; a node that is the last one waiting (everyone else deferring on it, or a partition heal with no new vertices) never re-runs the decision — I14's 'the event that should trigger recovery is the event the failure suppressed'.
design_fix: Drive WANTED population and try_commit from the node's own tick for every node role (observer included): a tick-scheduled `resolve_walk` over round_index[current−1..current+2] and a tick-scheduled try_commit independent of add_vertex. Add a test with an observer node that drops one vertex and asserts WANTED is populated and the hole admitted with zero inbound DAG_VERTEX traffic.
